findings.detail: ZReportArchive only signs and stores (signAndStore) or returns the stored signature verbatim from the archive (lines 72-80). There is no equivalent of the PHP ZReport::loadForSession (../pos/backend/services/ZReport.php:65-111) which re-computes the signature over the stored payload and sets verified = hash_equals(stored, recomputed), nor of the verify page (../pos/frontend/pages/sessions/z-report-verify.php) that renders OK / TAMPERED. The ZReportDialog merely displays the first 16 hex chars and the words 'tamper-evident' without ever validating anything. The entire purpose of an HMAC-signed archive — detecting after-the-fact tampering — is therefore not realized; a corrupted/edited row will be displayed as if authentic.
findings.recommendation: Add a verify() method that loads payload + signature_hex from z_report_archive, recomputes HMAC over the stored payload with secret(), compares with a constant-time equal (the hashes are equal-length hex; QMessageAuthenticationCode + a length-checked byte compare), and returns OK/UNSIGNED/TAMPERED. Surface the result in ZReportDialog (and any manager verify screen) the way the PHP verify page does.

findings.title: z_report_archive is not append-only in SQLite — claim of immutability is unenforced
findings.detail: The PHP/Postgres schema (../db/triggers/phase5_drap.sql:52-63) installs prevent_z_report_archive_modifications, a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that rejects any modification so the archive is genuinely append-only. The Qt migration v2 creates a plain table with only a UNIQUE(session_id) constraint and no triggers. The header comment (ZReportArchive.h:14-18) and Database.cpp:201 both assert the table is 'append-only', but nothing prevents UPDATE or DELETE. Combined with the missing verification path, an operator can edit payload + signature_hex (e.g. to hide a cash variance) with zero detection. This defeats the tamper-evidence guarantee the feature exists to provide.
findings.recommendation: Add SQLite BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE triggers on z_report_archive that RAISE(ABORT,...) (mirror the audit_log_immutable pattern already used elsewhere), shipped in a migration. Pair with the verify() method so even a direct-file tamper is caught at display time.

findings.title: Canonical payload diverges entirely from the PHP spec; signatures are non-portable and incomplete
findings.detail: PHP signs a ksorted JSON object of computed aggregates (cash/card/all totals net of refunds, refund counts and amounts, pharmacy_name, sale_receipts list, ISO-8601 normalized timestamps) using JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES|UNICODE and the shared cphc.audit_secret (../pos/backend/services/ZReport.php:113-235), explicitly documented as 'preserved byte-for-byte'. The Qt version instead pipe-joins ten raw cashier_sessions columns (total_cash_sales, total_refunds_paid, etc.) with no refund breakdown by mode, no receipts, no pharmacy_name, and a different secret. The two signatures can never match, and the Qt payload omits exactly the sale-level detail the PHP signature was meant to bind, so a report whose underlying sales rows were altered after close would still verify. CLAUDE.md treats deviations from the PHP spec as bugs.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) reproduce the PHP payload construction and JSON canonicalization so signatures are comparable and bind the full report content, or (b) explicitly document this as a single-PC simplification in CLAUDE.md/PHP_APP_MAP.md and at minimum include the per-receipt totals and refund breakdown in the signed payload so tampering with sales is detectable.

findings.title: Key file written world-readable before chmod (TOCTOU window) and excluded from hardenPermissions
findings.detail: secret() creates zreport.key by f.write(key.toHex()) and only afterward calls f.setPermissions(ReadOwner|WriteOwner). Between creation and the chmod the file exists with the process umask (typically 0644) — another local user can read the signing key in that window. AppPaths::hardenPermissions() (src/domain/AppPaths.cpp:41-54) only re-tightens the DB and its WAL/SHM sidecars and the base dir; it never touches zreport.key, so if the chmod step is skipped (e.g. the open at line 34 fails but a prior partial file exists) the key can remain readable. The base-dir 0700 mitigates this on Linux but the key file itself is the actual signing secret and should be 0600 in its own right.
findings.recommendation: Create the file with restrictive permissions before writing (set permissions on an empty file, or open O_EXCL and chmod first), and add zreport.key to AppPaths::hardenPermissions() so every launch re-asserts 0600.

findings.title: Z-report generation writes no audit_log entry
findings.detail: PHP's ZReport::generate writes Audit::write(generatedBy, 'Z_REPORT_GENERATED', 'cashier_sessions', sessionId, ..., {signature_hex, archive_id}) (../pos/backend/services/ZReport.php:49-50). The Qt signAndStore inserts into z_report_archive but never records a Z_REPORT_GENERATED audit event, so the who/when of the day-close stamp is missing from the audit trail that CLAUDE.md requires for sales and stock/day-close actions. Compounding this, ZReportDialog passes userId 0 (ZReportDialog.cpp:104-105), so generated_by is stored NULL — the archive itself cannot attribute the report to a user.
findings.recommendation: Plumb the current user id into ZReportDialog and write a Z_REPORT_GENERATED audit entry (with signature_hex and archive id) inside the same transaction as the insert; stop signing with userId 0.

findings.title: signAndStore performs a non-transactional read-then-insert with no audit/insert atomicity
findings.detail: The method does a SELECT for an existing row, then a separate INSERT OR IGNORE, with no enclosing transaction. The UNIQUE(session_id) constraint plus INSERT OR IGNORE makes a duplicate row impossible, so this is benign today; but if the audit-log write (recommended above) is added it must be atomic with the insert, and a concurrent caller could currently get res.ok=true with fromArchive=false while its INSERT was silently ignored (returning a signature it did not actually persist if the stored payload differs — e.g. if canonicalPayload were ever made time-dependent). CLAUDE.md mandates transactions around multi-statement changes.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the existence check, insert, and any audit write in a single transaction; after INSERT OR IGNORE, re-SELECT the stored signature_hex so the returned value always reflects what is actually persisted.

findings.title: Missing tests for signature stability, tamper detection, and key persistence/permissions
findings.detail: The only Z-report test checks idempotency (same signature on second call, exactly one row, 64-hex length). There is no test that (a) the signature matches a known expected value for a fixed payload+key (so a refactor of canonicalPayload silently changing the signed bytes would go unnoticed), (b) editing the stored payload causes verification to fail (there is no verify path to test), or (c) zreport.key is generated with 0600 permissions and is reused across instantiations rather than regenerated (a regenerated key would invalidate all prior signatures). Given CLAUDE.md mandates tests on tamper-evidence-class paths, this coverage is insufficient.
findings.recommendation: Add tests: a known-answer HMAC vector for a fixed payload and key; a tamper test that mutates payload (once an immutability trigger and verify() exist, assert verify returns TAMPERED / the trigger rejects the UPDATE); and a key-persistence test asserting the file is created once with owner-only permissions.

findings.title: Brittle key-file path built with '/../' relative segment
findings.detail: secret() locates the key via QDir(AppPaths::logosDir()).filePath('../zreport.key'), i.e. it intentionally walks up out of the logos subdir to land in the app-data base dir. This couples the key location to the relative structure of logosDir() and is unobvious; if logosDir() were ever changed to not be a direct child of baseDir the key would silently move (orphaning existing signatures). The base dir is already known to AppPaths but not exposed.
findings.recommendation: Expose an AppPaths::dataDir()/baseDir() (or a dedicated keyFilePath()) accessor and resolve zreport.key directly under it, instead of relying on a '../' traversal from logosDir().

findings.title: WAL checkpoint result is never checked; backup can silently be stale or inconsistent
findings.detail: In backupNow() (BackupService.cpp:27) the checkpoint is issued as `QSqlQuery(m_db).exec("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)")` with the return value and result row discarded. wal_checkpoint can fail or only partially complete (e.g. another read/write transaction holds a read lock, returning a non-zero busy code and leaving frames in the -wal). When that happens the subsequent QFile::copy of the main .sqlite file copies a snapshot that is MISSING the un-checkpointed WAL frames — i.e. a backup that silently omits the most recent committed sales/stock movements. For a pharmacy whose records 'aren't recoverable if lost' (per the header comment) this is a correctness-of-record bug, not just a nicety. The TRUNCATE variant also requires no other connection to be reading; in a single-PC app that is usually true, but auto-backup fires on startup while the rest of the app is initializing.
findings.recommendation: Run the checkpoint via a QSqlQuery you keep, check exec() returned true, read the result row (busy, log frames, checkpointed frames) and treat busy!=0 or checkpointed<log as a failure (retry with PASSIVE/FULL or abort the backup with a clear error). At minimum, fail the backup if the checkpoint pragma returns an error instead of proceeding to copy.

findings.title: No restore capability exists despite 'records not recoverable if lost' mandate
findings.detail: BackupService (and the whole codebase — grep for 'restore' finds only stock-restore on voids) offers only backupNow/autoBackupIfDue. There is no UI or service to restore a backup file into the live DB. Recovery requires an operator to manually locate the AppDataLocation directory, stop the app, and copy/rename a .sqlite file over the live DB (and delete stale -wal/-shm sidecars, which they won't know to do). For a single-PC medical system this makes the backup feature only half-implemented: it protects data but provides no tested, safe path to actually use it under pressure.
findings.recommendation: Add a restore flow (validate the chosen file is a well-formed SQLite DB with the expected schema/user_version, close the live connection, atomically replace the DB file AND remove -wal/-shm sidecars, re-open). Cover with a test that backs up, mutates, restores, and verifies the original state returns.

findings.title: Backup files written with default world-readable permissions; leaks bcrypt PINs and sale data
findings.detail: AppPaths::hardenPermissions() locks the live DB and its -wal/-shm to owner-only 0600 (AppPaths.cpp:41-53), but the backup copy produced by QFile::copy (BackupService.cpp:32) inherits the destination filesystem's default umask permissions and is never hardened. Backups contain the full users table (bcrypt PIN hashes), audit_log, and all sales/patient records, and the design explicitly targets removable USB / network shares — exactly the high-exposure destinations. The copy of the most sensitive file in the system is the least protected.
findings.recommendation: After a successful QFile::copy, call QFile::setPermissions(dest, ReadOwner|WriteOwner). Note removable/FAT media may not honor POSIX perms — warn the operator in that case, and consider documenting/encouraging an encrypted destination.

findings.title: Backup assumes dbFilePath() equals the open connection's file and ignores -wal/-shm
findings.detail: backupNow copies AppPaths::dbFilePath() (BackupService.cpp:29) rather than m_db.databaseName(). These are normally the same, but the source is the only place that knows the actual open file; if the app ever opens a non-default path (legacy migration in AppPaths copies a DB, tests, multi-profile) the backup would copy the wrong/empty file. Separately, because the copy relies entirely on the checkpoint having fully folded the WAL, it deliberately does NOT copy the -wal/-shm sidecars — which is correct ONLY if the checkpoint fully succeeded (see the unchecked-checkpoint finding). The two issues compound: an incomplete checkpoint plus a sidecar-less copy = silent data loss with no error surfaced.
findings.recommendation: Source the path from m_db.databaseName() (fall back to dbFilePath()). Either guarantee a fully-successful TRUNCATE checkpoint before copying, or copy the -wal/-shm sidecars alongside the main file so the backup is self-consistent regardless of checkpoint state.

findings.title: Auto-backup runs synchronously on the UI thread at startup and swallows all failures
findings.detail: MainWindow.cpp:209-215 calls autoBackupIfDue during window construction on the GUI thread. Copying a large DB to a slow/absent USB or unreachable network share blocks the UI from appearing (frozen window) for the duration, or stalls on a stale mount. autoBackupIfDue (BackupService.cpp:41-65) returns plain bool and discards the Result.error on failure, so a destination that is full, unmounted, or permission-denied produces NO feedback — the operator believes auto-backup is protecting them when it has been silently failing for days. last_backup_at is (correctly) only updated on success, so it keeps retrying, but the user never learns why backups aren't appearing.
findings.recommendation: Run the auto-backup off the UI thread (or after the window is shown) and surface failures: keep the Result, log the error, and show a non-blocking warning/status when a due auto-backup fails. Consider a short timeout / reachability check before copying to a network share.

findings.title: No retention/pruning: backups accumulate unbounded and can fill the destination
findings.detail: Each backup is written to a unique timestamped filename (BackupService.cpp:30) and nothing ever deletes old ones. With daily auto-backups to a USB stick, the destination grows without limit until it fills, at which point QFile::copy fails — and (per the prior finding) that failure is silently swallowed for auto-backups, so backups simply stop with no notice. The QFile::remove(dest) at line 31 only removes a same-second collision, not old backups.
findings.recommendation: Add a retention policy (keep last N or last N days) and prune older backups after a successful copy, or at least surface available-space / copy-failure errors so the operator knows to clear space.

findings.title: Critical paths untested: WAL-fold consistency, 24h gating, and failure modes
findings.detail: The only coverage (tests/smoke.cpp:336-359) checks that backupNow copies a file that opens and has >=1 user. It does NOT test: (1) that data committed only in the WAL is actually present in the backup (the core correctness claim of the checkpoint), (2) autoBackupIfDue gating — that it skips when last_backup_at < 24h, runs when stale/missing, and is a no-op when AutoBackup!='1' or BackupDir empty, (3) failure modes — empty destDir, non-creatable directory, copy-into-read-only/full destination returning r.error. Given CLAUDE.md mandates tests on data-integrity paths and this is net-new code with no PHP reference, the consistency and gating logic is unverified.
findings.recommendation: Add tests: insert a row, do NOT checkpoint manually, run backupNow, open the copy and assert the row is present (proves the WAL fold). Add gating tests by manipulating LastBackupAt/AutoBackup/BackupDir settings. Add negative tests asserting r.ok==false and a populated r.error for bad destinations.

findings.title: Auto-backup updates last_backup_at with caller-supplied nowIso, drifting from the checkpoint moment
findings.detail: autoBackupIfDue records settings.set(LastBackupAt, nowIso) (BackupService.cpp:61) using the timestamp passed in by the caller at the start, and the 24h comparison parses both last and now from ISO strings (lines 53-54). If QDateTime::fromString fails to parse a stored value (e.g. format drift, or an entry written by backupNow in AdminPage which also uses Qt::ISODate — consistent today but two separate call sites), lastDt.isValid() is false and the guard silently falls through to backing up every startup. The timestamp source is also injected rather than taken at the actual backup instant, making the 'last backup' record slightly inaccurate and the logic dependent on two callers agreeing on format.
findings.recommendation: Centralize the timestamp/format in one place (or capture it inside the service at the copy moment), and decide explicitly what an unparseable last_backup_at should mean (treat as 'due' is acceptable but should be intentional and commented).

findings.title: Receipt omits batch number, expiry, generic, unit-of-measure detail, customer block, and void/refund/reprint banner
findings.detail: EscPos.php::receipt prints, per line, the generic name + strength, a unit-of-measure line ('2 x STRIP (10 TABLET each = 20 TABLET)'), and 'Batch:<n>  Exp:mm/yy'. It also prints a customer block (name/phone/CNIC when present) and a prominent status banner ('*** VOIDED — NOT A VALID SALE ***', '*** REFUNDED IN FULL ***', '** PARTIALLY REFUNDED **') plus a '-- REPRINT --' marker (EscPos.php:104-127, 168-189). The Qt SaleResultLine only carries name/qty/unitLabel/unitMrp/lineTotal and EscPosHeader has no customer/status/reprint fields, so EscPosRenderer cannot emit any of this. Batch+expiry on the printed receipt is a pharmacy traceability requirement, and a reprinted refunded/voided sale will print as if it were a valid live sale.
findings.recommendation: Extend SaleResultLine with genericName, strength, batchNumber, expiryDate, soldUnitFactor, qtyInBaseUnits, baseUnit, and add customer fields + status + isReprint to EscPosHeader. Reproduce the EscPos.php line/banner logic exactly and cover it with a byte-for-byte golden test against PHP output.

findings.title: PRICE column uses per-base-unit MRP, not per-sold-unit price (qty x price != line total for packs)
findings.detail: EscPos.php:155-156 computes the displayed price as effPrice = unitMrp * soldFactor so the PRICE column shows per-sold-unit price (per strip/box) and qty x price reads naturally against the line total. The Qt renderer prints money2(item.unitMrp) directly (per base unit). When an item is sold as a pack (soldFactor > 1) the printed price column will not multiply out to the line total, confusing the customer and diverging from PHP. The Qt model also has no soldUnitFactor to perform the multiply.
findings.recommendation: Carry soldUnitFactor in SaleResultLine and print money2(unitMrp * factor) like PHP; verify against a golden receipt where a pack item is sold.

findings.title: Print and self-test actions are not written to the audit trail
findings.detail: Printer.php audits every print path: PRINT_SUCCESS/PRINT_FAILED, RECEIPT_REPRINTED/RECEIPT_REPRINT_FAILED, PRINTER_SELFTEST_OK/PRINTER_SELFTEST_FAILED, ZREPORT_PRINTED/_FAILED (Printer.php:121-133, 142-150). The Qt receipt print and self-test paths only show a QMessageBox and write nothing to audit_log (AuditRepository is used in AdminPage only for user management at line 678, never on print). CLAUDE.md requires reproducing who-did-what-when; a failed or repeated receipt print currently leaves no record.
findings.recommendation: On every printRaw result, write an audit row (action, target sales/Printer, queue, error, reprint flag) mirroring Printer.php verbs.

findings.title: row() truncates the right-justified value, diverging from PHP byte output on long values
findings.detail: The Qt row() wraps its result in clip(label + spaces + value, Width), so when label.length()+value.length() >= Width it drops trailing characters of the right-hand value. EscPos.php::row (EscPos.php:364-368) never clips — it uses max(1, w - len(left) - len(right)) and returns the full string, letting an over-long row exceed the width (the printer wraps it). For long invoice numbers or 'Cash Tendered:' rows this produces different bytes than PHP and can silently chop the amount.
findings.recommendation: Drop the clip() wrapper in row() to match PHP exactly; only the min-1-space rule should apply.

findings.title: Z-report thermal rendering is not ported
findings.detail: EscPos.php::zReport (EscPos.php:265-356) renders a full end-of-shift Z-report (cash drawer reconciliation, sales recap, per-receipt list, signature_short) to the 80mm printer, invoked by Printer::printZReport. The Qt EscPosRenderer implements only receipt() and selfTest() — there is no zReport equivalent (grep confirms none), so a cashier cannot print an end-of-shift Z ticket from the native app.
findings.recommendation: Port EscPos::zReport including the refunds-paid derivation and the *REF*/*VOID* receipt markers; cover with a golden test.

findings.title: Width math counts UTF-16 code units, not display columns
findings.detail: clip/padLeft/padRight/row use QString::length() (UTF-16 code units). PHP uses mb_strlen/mb_substr with explicit UTF-8. For ASCII pharmacy data the column alignment matches, but any non-ASCII character in pharmacy name/address/medicine name will misalign columns or mis-clip vs PHP. Lower risk given the data is English, but it is a latent divergence the tests will not catch.
findings.recommendation: Document the ASCII assumption or normalize on code-point counts; at minimum add a test with a multibyte pharmacy name to confirm acceptable behavior.

findings.title: Receipt/self-test tests are substring-only; CUPS layer has no tests
findings.detail: The only receipt test asserts bytes.contains('CITY CARE'), 'PAYABLE', the receipt number, init/cut bytes, and size>100. It never compares the full byte stream to a PHP-generated golden fixture, so layout/padding/price/banner divergences (findings above) pass silently. selfTest() is untested. CupsStatus parsing (lpstat/lpinfo regexes, usbPrinters, driverInstalled fallbacks) and CupsRawPrinter argv construction / error surfacing have no tests at all, despite CLAUDE.md requiring tests on anything touching pricing/quantities and matching PHP bit-for-bit.
findings.recommendation: Generate golden ESC/POS fixtures from EscPos.php for representative sales (pack item, discount, refunded/reprint, customer block) and assert byte equality. Add table-driven tests for CupsStatus::usbPrinters / listQueues line parsing using captured fixture output.

findings.title: Self-test ticket omits PPD/time/model lines and hardcodes Status:OK
findings.detail: EscPos.php::selfTest prints model ('Black Copper BC-88AC'), 'PPD: zjiang/zj80.ppd', a 'Time: <iso8601>' line, and 'Status: OK'. The Qt selfTest prints only Queue + 'Status: OK'. The self-test is the operator's primary 'is the printer wired up' diagnostic; dropping the timestamp/PPD/model lines makes a printed ticket less useful for field troubleshooting. 'Status: OK' is also a literal constant in both, so it reflects nothing about actual device health.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the PHP self-test fields (model, PPD, local timestamp). Consider folding in the live CupsSnapshot (driver/queue) so the printed ticket reflects real status rather than a constant.

findings.title: Controlled-substance / Rx schedule badges dropped from alternatives
findings.detail: The PHP source selects m.controlled_schedule and m.prescription_required, and pos-search-results.php renders a red 'NARCOTIC' badge and a 'SCHEDULE G/H' warning badge for each alternative (medicine-alternatives.php lines 47-49, pos-search-results.php lines 41-44). The Qt port's AlternativeMedicine struct has no controlled_schedule/prescription_required fields, the SELECT never reads them, and the dialog shows only Brand/Strength/Form/Manufacturer/On hand/MRP. When a cashier substitutes one brand for another, they lose the visual warning that the alternative is a narcotic or scheduled drug — a meaningful safety/compliance regression in a medical retail system.
findings.recommendation: Add controlled_schedule (and optionally prescription_required) to the query and the AlternativeMedicine struct, and render a colored badge column in AlternativesDialog mirroring the PHP badge--danger/badge--warning styling from theme.qss.

findings.title: No tests for the alternatives generic/stock/expiry/pricing logic
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md mandates that anything touching quantities, pricing, batch numbers, and expiry be covered by tests comparing against PHP behavior. AlternativesFinder sums saleable on-hand across valid batches and picks the soonest-expiry MRP — exactly that kind of logic — yet there is no test file. tests/ contains barcode, printing, smoke and screenshots only. Regressions in the batch-validity predicate (quarantine/expired/expiry-date filters), the FEFO MRP pick, or the ranking would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add an alternatives_test.cpp that seeds medicines + batches (quarantined, expired, past-expiry, multi-batch same-generic) and asserts on_hand sums, the soonest-expiry MRP selection, self-exclusion, case-insensitive generic match, and ranking order against expected PHP results.

findings.title: Source medicine not gated on is_active / deleted_at (parity deviation)
findings.detail: PHP resolves the source generic with 'WHERE id = :id AND is_active = TRUE AND deleted_at IS NULL' (medicine-alternatives.php lines 35-37); if the source is inactive/soft-deleted it returns no generic and the 'no generic name' message. The Qt query is 'SELECT generic_name FROM medicines WHERE id = ?' with no active/deleted guard, so a soft-deleted or deactivated medicine will still produce a populated alternatives list. Behavioral divergence from the source-of-truth spec.
findings.recommendation: Add 'AND is_active = 1 AND deleted_at IS NULL' to the source-medicine generic lookup to match PHP.

findings.title: Missing LIMIT 20 cap present in the PHP query
findings.detail: PHP caps the alternatives result at 'LIMIT 20' (medicine-alternatives.php line 64). The Qt query has no LIMIT, so for a very common generic (e.g. paracetamol) it will return and render every matching brand. Functionally minor but a parity deviation and a small unbounded-result/perf concern in the dialog.
findings.recommendation: Append 'LIMIT 20' to the query (or a documented intentionally-higher cap) to match PHP semantics.

findings.title: expiry_date comparison uses date('now') (UTC) — midnight boundary skew
findings.detail: Both the on-hand SUM and MRP subqueries compare 'b.expiry_date > date('now')'. SQLite date('now') is UTC, whereas PHP's CURRENT_DATE is the Postgres server's (local) date. For a single-PC AlmaLinux deployment east of UTC, near local midnight a batch expiring 'today' could be filtered differently than PHP would. This matches BatchRepository's FEFO query so it is internally consistent, but it is a systemic UTC-vs-local issue that could make the alternatives list show a different on-hand/MRP than the actual sellable stock for a few hours a day.
findings.recommendation: Standardize the app on a single 'today' definition (e.g. date('now','localtime') or a bound app-supplied local date) across FEFO and AlternativesFinder, and document the choice.

findings.title: Dialog Close button wired to accept() instead of reject()
findings.detail: QDialogButtonBox(Close) emits rejected(), and it is correctly connected to QDialog::accept here, so closing works — but connecting the Close button to accept() (rather than reject/close) is semantically backwards and easy to break if more buttons are added later. The dialog is read-only so behavior is fine today; flagging for clarity.
findings.recommendation: Connect rejected() to QDialog::reject (or just call QDialog::close) for semantic clarity; result code is irrelevant for this read-only dialog.

findings.title: POS allows completing a sale with no open cashier shift (PHP blocks it)
findings.detail: The PHP terminal computes $hasOpenShift = Sessions::currentFor($cashierId) !== null (terminal.php:453-454) and renders the Complete-sale CTA disabled with a 'No open shift' blocked reason whenever there is none (terminal.php:1213-1221, plus the banner at line 797-801). PosTerminalPage never queries SessionRepository::openSessionId and never disables m_complete; completeSale() proceeds unconditionally. SaleService::commit silently inserts the sale with sessionId = openSessionId() which returns 0/null when no shift is open (SaleService.cpp:208,345 bumpForSale is a no-op), so a cashier with no shift can ring up sales that are never attributed to or reconciled in any cashier_sessions row. This breaks Z-report/reconciliation parity and the intended 'sales are blocked until you open a shift' control.
findings.recommendation: On construction and after each completed sale, query SessionRepository::openSessionId(m_userId); if 0, disable m_complete (and ideally Park) and show a 'No open cashier shift — open one to sell' banner, mirroring terminal.php:1213-1221. Optionally also have SaleService refuse to commit when no session is open if the PHP service is intended to require one.

findings.title: Complete-sale button not gated on cash tendered ≥ grand total
findings.detail: For CASH payment the server (SaleService.cpp:119-121, matching Sale.php:155-158) rejects amount_tendered < grand_total with 'Cash sale requires amount tendered ≥ grand total.' The UI computes and shows Change in recompute() but never reflects an underpayment state: m_complete stays enabled and the cashier only learns of the shortfall via a QMessageBox after pressing Complete (after possibly also clearing the controlled/discount PIN prompts). The PHP terminal surfaces this as part of its sticky blocked CTA. This is a worse cashier experience under the most common (cash) payment path.
findings.recommendation: In recompute(), when paymentMode==CASH and tendered < grand (or tendered blank), disable m_complete and show an inline 'Insufficient cash tendered' hint; re-enable once tendered ≥ grand. Keep the server-side check as the backstop.

findings.title: Park/resume stores the pack label into ParkedItem.baseUnit, mislabeling resumed pack lines
findings.detail: parkBill() does items.push_back({c.medicineId, c.name, c.unitLabel, c.unitMrp, c.qty * c.factor}). ParkedItem field order is {medicineId, name, baseUnit, unitMrp, qty} (ParkedCartRepository.h:10-17), so c.unitLabel is written into the baseUnit slot. When a line was added as a pack, c.unitLabel is the purchase unit (e.g. 'BOX'), not the base unit. resumeBill() then reconstructs the CartLine with factor 1 and unitLabel = it.baseUnit, so the resumed line displays the pack label with factor 1. Quantity and money are correct (parked as base units at per-base MRP), so this is a display/label parity bug only — but it can confuse a cashier who parked '1 BOX of 100' and resumes seeing '100 BOX'.
findings.recommendation: Park base lines with the medicine's actual base unit label (e.g. store the base unit, not c.unitLabel), or carry factor+label through the parked schema so pack lines resume with their original sold-unit presentation. At minimum write the true base unit into the baseUnit field.

findings.title: Discount-exceeds-subtotal not surfaced until after PIN prompt and commit
findings.detail: recompute() clamps grand to zero when discount > subtotal (line 389-391), so the UI shows Grand total 0.00 and a fully-paid-looking state. SaleService.cpp:95-97 (matching Sale.php:135-136) rejects discount > subtotal with 'Discount cannot exceed subtotal'. Because the discount is positive, completeSale() will first open the manager-override PIN dialog (lines 465-480) and only after a successful override hit the server, which then rejects the sale. The cashier (and a summoned manager) burn a PIN entry before learning the discount was invalid.
findings.recommendation: In recompute()/completeSale(), validate discount ≤ subtotal before showing the override dialog and disable Complete (or show an inline error) when the discount exceeds the subtotal, mirroring the server rule.

findings.title: Search fires a DB query on every keystroke with no debounce
findings.detail: m_search's textChanged is wired directly to runSearch(), which calls MedicineRepository::searchForPos on the UI thread and rebuilds the results table for every character. A barcode scanner that injects a full code rapidly (then Enter) triggers one query+table rebuild per character; on the ~318-row seed this is tolerable but unnecessary, and it scales poorly as the catalog grows. There is no minimum-length guard or timer-based debounce.
findings.recommendation: Add a short single-shot QTimer debounce (e.g. 120-200 ms) before issuing the query, and/or skip querying for queries below a minimum length, so a fast scan results in a single search. Keep returnPressed handling for immediate scan completion.

findings.title: Change amount displayed even for non-cash payment modes
findings.detail: recompute() computes and shows a Change value whenever Tendered is non-empty, regardless of payment mode. For CARD/OTHER the PHP flow does not require tendered and 'change' is not a meaningful concept; showing a Tendered/Change pair for a card sale invites the cashier to mis-enter a tender and is a small parity drift from the cash-centric PHP checkout. There is also no reaction in recompute() to m_payment changing (no connect on currentIndexChanged), so the Change/validation never updates when the cashier switches payment mode.
findings.recommendation: Connect m_payment::currentIndexChanged to recompute(), and hide/disable the Tendered and Change rows (or zero them) when payment mode is not CASH.

findings.title: No automated test exercises the POS terminal cart/checkout UI flow
findings.detail: Money/stock/FEFO/discount/parked paths are well covered at the service/domain layer (salecalc_tests, sale_tests, fefo_tests, parked_tests). However the UI-side translation logic — pack factor folding (qty × factor → base units), cart merge keyed on medicineId+factor, park-as-base-units and resume reconstruction, and the controlled/discount prompt gating decisions — lives in PosTerminalPage with no test. The park/resume label bug above is exactly the kind of regression a thin headless test of the cart-to-SaleInput / cart-to-ParkedItem mapping would catch.
findings.recommendation: Extract the cart→SaleInput and cart→ParkedItem mapping (and the prompt-required predicates) into small testable helpers or a controller class, and add cases covering pack factor folding, merge rules, and park/resume round-trip so the UI math stays bit-for-bit with the service expectations.

findings.title: On-hand stock query diverges from PHP (extra expiry_date filter)
findings.detail: The PHP catalog list computes on-hand as SUM(current_qty) WHERE current_qty>0 AND is_quarantined=FALSE AND is_expired=FALSE (medicines.php:343-344) — it does NOT filter on expiry_date. The Qt list() adds an extra clause: "AND b.expiry_date > date('now')". So a batch whose expiry has passed but whose is_expired flag has not yet been flipped (the flag is maintained separately by batch logic) is counted by PHP but excluded by Qt. Two screens over the same data will show different 'On hand' numbers, and the Medicines list will disagree with other inventory screens. searchForPos() (line 237-241) uses the same extra filter, but that is the POS path where excluding past-expiry is arguably intended; the catalog list must mirror PHP exactly.
findings.recommendation: Drop "AND b.expiry_date > date('now')" from the list() on-hand subquery so it matches the PHP definition (rely on is_expired/is_quarantined like PHP). If past-expiry-but-unflagged stock should be excluded, change it in PHP first and port deliberately — the source-of-truth must win. Add a test asserting on-hand counts a non-quarantined, non-is_expired batch regardless of expiry_date.

findings.title: Soft-deleted SKU/barcode auto-restore workflow not ported
findings.detail: PHP medicines.php (lines 156-196, 224) implements a deliberate workflow: when you 'Add' a medicine whose SKU or barcode collides with a SOFT-DELETED row, it does NOT error — it resurrects that row (clears deleted_at), applies the new data, KEEPS THE ORIGINAL id so batches/sales/audit references keep resolving, and writes a MEDICINE_RESTORED audit event. It also refuses with a clear message if the SKU and barcode point to two DIFFERENT deleted rows. The Qt port has none of this: skuInUse()/barcodeInUse() only check live rows (deleted_at IS NULL), so a colliding soft-deleted SKU passes validation and create() does a fresh INSERT, producing a NEW id and a new orphaned catalog entry. The old medicine's historical references stay attached to the dead row, defeating the entire point of soft delete. There is also no MEDICINE_RESTORED audit action.
findings.recommendation: Port the auto-restore path: in create() (or before it), look up any soft-deleted row matching sku/barcode; if found, convert to an UPDATE that clears deleted_at on that id and writes a MEDICINE_RESTORED audit row; refuse if sku and barcode resolve to two distinct deleted ids. Surface the 'restored from trash' message in MedicineDialog. Add tests for restore + the two-different-rows refusal.

findings.title: Create/update mutation + audit write are not wrapped in a transaction
findings.detail: create(), update(), and softDelete() each run the medicines DML and then call Audit::write() as two independent statements with no surrounding transaction. CLAUDE.md mandates 'wrap every multi-statement change in a transaction'. If the audit insert fails (or the process is killed between the two), you get a catalog mutation with no audit record — the opposite of the append-only who-did-what-when guarantee the project requires. PHP runs these inside its request/connection but the porting brief explicitly calls out transactional integrity for stock/audit paths.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each mutating method in db.transaction()/commit() with rollback on any failure (including Audit::write returning false), so the medicine change and its audit row commit atomically.

findings.title: Length and negative-value validations from PHP are missing in the dialog
findings.detail: PHP validates max lengths server-side (brand/generic <=160, sku <=40) and rejects negative reorder_level / reorder_quantity with friendly messages (medicines.php:132-142). The Qt dialog relies solely on QLineEdit::setMaxLength (silent truncation, no message) for lengths, and QSpinBox min=0 prevents negatives in the UI — but the repository itself performs NO server-side length/negative validation, so any non-UI caller (or a future programmatic path) can insert over-long or invalid values. Behavior also differs: PHP tells the user 'Brand name is too long'; Qt silently truncates at 160 with no feedback.
findings.recommendation: Add the same length/negative checks in MedicineDialog::accept() (or, better, in a shared MedicineRepository validate() so the rule lives in the domain layer per CLAUDE.md), matching PHP messages. Keep maxLength as a convenience but don't rely on it as the sole guard.

findings.title: Edit dialog silently shows an empty form when the medicine can't be loaded
findings.detail: When m_editId != 0, the dialog calls m_repo->find(m_editId, &d) but ignores a false return (e.g. the row was soft-deleted or deleted in another path between list load and edit click). The dialog then opens with default/blank fields and the title 'Edit medicine'; if the user clicks Save it will run update() against an id whose row no longer satisfies deleted_at IS NULL, so the UPDATE affects 0 rows yet update() still returns true (it only checks exec success, not rowsAffected) and reports success. The user believes they edited a record that no longer exists.
findings.recommendation: If find() returns false in the constructor, show a message and reject()/close the dialog. Separately, have update()/softDelete() check query.numRowsAffected() and return false when 0 rows matched, so stale edits/deletes surface as errors instead of silent no-ops.

findings.title: MedicineDialog has no automated/UI test; validation branches untested
findings.detail: medicine_tests.cpp exercises the repository thoroughly, but the dialog's accept() validation logic (required-field checks, OTHER-requires-custom-form rule at line 199, form validity, friendly SKU/barcode-in-use messaging, save dispatch between create vs update) has zero coverage. These are exactly the add/edit validation rules the audit task flags as in-scope, and they currently can only be regression-checked manually. The 'OTHER form requires form_custom' rule in particular exists only in the dialog (the repo accepts an empty form_custom), so a repo-only test cannot catch a regression there.
findings.recommendation: Add a thin testable validation function (free function or static MedicineRepository::validate(MedicineDraft, errorOut)) covering required fields, OTHER->form_custom, units>=1, length/negative limits, and call it from accept(). Cover it in tests so dialog rules are verified without driving Qt widgets.

findings.title: PHP medicines list shows a packs-conversion hint that the Qt list drops
findings.detail: The PHP list renders on-hand as 'N base_unit' plus a secondary line '≈ P purchase_unit + R base_unit' when units_per_purchase>1 (medicines.php:1071-1079), helping staff read stock as whole packs + loose units. The Qt list shows only '%1 %2'.arg(onHand, baseUnit) — the packs breakdown is gone even though MedicineRow already carries purchaseUnit and unitsPerPurchase. Minor visual/parity loss on a screen meant to feel identical to the web app. PHP also shows a Manufacturer column that the Qt table omits.
findings.recommendation: Append the '≈ packs + remainder' hint when unitsPerPurchase>1 and onHand>0 (intdiv/modulo, same as PHP), and consider adding the Manufacturer column to match the web layout.

findings.title: Search differs from PHP: no barcode-scan exact match in catalog list
findings.detail: PHP's catalog search (medicines.php:309-334) runs the typed text through QrParser and, for a scanned GS1/GTIN barcode, does an EXACT match on primary_barcode against the 14-digit GTIN, the 13-digit (leading-zero-stripped), and the raw string, and surfaces a 'barcode chip'. The Qt catalog list() only does a LIKE substring match on brand/generic/sku/manufacturer/primary_barcode. (Note searchForPos() DOES implement the GTIN-14/13 exact match, so the parsing exists — it's just not wired into the catalog list.) Scanning a barcode on the Medicines screen will therefore LIKE-match the full raw scan string and likely miss the medicine, whereas PHP resolves it.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the Barcode::parse + GTIN-14/13 IN(...) logic from searchForPos() in list() so scanning a barcode on the catalog screen exact-matches the medicine like PHP does (optionally surface the parsed-barcode chip).

findings.title: Stock adjustments skip the mandatory manager-PIN re-confirmation that PHP enforces
findings.detail: PHP adjustments.php gates every adjustment behind ManagerOverride::verify($pin, 'stock_adjustment') and throws if the PIN is missing/invalid, with an explicit comment that this 'protects against unattended workstations being used to write off stock'. The Qt AdjustmentsPage::applyAdjustment() calls StockAdjuster::adjust(...) directly with no PIN prompt at all — anyone sitting at an unlocked manager session (or any non-cashier who can reach the Inventory tab) can write off arbitrary quantities/value of stock with zero re-auth. The building block exists: ManagerOverrideDialog + UserRepository::verifyManagerOverride are already used by PosTerminalPage and ReturnsPage, so this is a missing wiring, not missing infrastructure. This is a direct security-control regression versus the source-of-truth spec on a money/stock path.
findings.recommendation: Before calling StockAdjuster::adjust, present ManagerOverrideDialog and verify via UserRepository::verifyManagerOverride(pin, m_userId, "stock_adjustment") (allowing self-confirm, matching PHP), aborting the adjustment if it fails. Cover with a test that an adjustment without a valid PIN is rejected.

findings.title: Adjustment picker omits quarantined-but-empty batches and never enforces the EXPIRY_WRITEOFF-only rule for quarantined stock
findings.detail: PHP loads the batch list with WHERE b.current_qty > 0 OR b.is_quarantined = TRUE, so quarantined batches sitting at zero (or any) qty are still adjustable for write-off. The Qt batchesForMedicine() loads ALL batches for the medicine regardless of state with no filter, which is a superset but changes which rows appear and their ordering versus PHP (PHP orders brand_name then expiry; Qt orders expiry then id). More importantly, the StockAdjuster header documents a rule that a QUARANTINED batch may only be touched when reason == EXPIRY_WRITEOFF, but the UI gives no hint of this and lets the user pick any reason for a quarantined batch — the only feedback is a post-hoc 'Adjustment rejected' QMessageBox. The UI should reflect the same constraints the domain enforces so the operator isn't surprised.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the PHP batch query (current_qty>0 OR is_quarantined) and ordering, and disable/auto-select EXPIRY_WRITEOFF (or warn inline) when a quarantined batch is selected so the UI matches the domain rule. Verify against StockAdjuster.php's quarantine branch.

findings.title: Live cost-impact / after-adjustment preview from PHP is not ported
findings.detail: PHP adjustments.php renders a live preview block (current on-hand, after-adjustment with red highlight if it would go negative, cost per unit, and cost impact = abs(delta) x cost) that recomputes on batch/qty change before the operator commits. The Qt form has a batch combo, direction, qty, reason, notes and an Apply button but no preview — the operator only learns the cost impact and whether stock went negative after submitting. On a value/stock-write-off screen this preview is a meaningful safety/parity feature, especially since the result drives audit-logged cost impact.
findings.recommendation: Add a small preview area (current, after, cost/unit, cost impact) bound to batch/direction/qty changes, computing cost impact via Money (scale-2) to match the recorded value; highlight negative-resulting after-qty.

findings.title: Expiry-status badge ladder (business-rule thresholds) lives in an untestable anonymous namespace and has no test
findings.detail: statusFor() encodes the EXPIRED/QUARANTINED/CONFIRM(<=30d)/AMBER(<=60d)/INFO(<=90d)/OK ladder and its precedence (expired-or-days<=0 beats quarantined beats day-windows) — a direct port of stock.php's badge branch and exactly the kind of expiry/quarantine logic CLAUDE.md says must be ported exactly AND covered by tests. It is a file-local function in an anonymous namespace, so it cannot be unit-tested, and inventory_tests.cpp only covers the repository windows, not this ladder. A future tweak to a threshold (e.g. <=30 vs <30) would silently diverge from PHP with no test catching it.
findings.recommendation: Extract the status ladder into a free function in a shared header (e.g. domain/ExpiryStatus.h) and add a table-driven test covering each boundary (days = -1, 0, 30, 31, 60, 61, 90, 91) plus the expired/quarantined precedence, mirroring stock.php.

findings.title: expiringSoon has no lower date bound, so past-expiry batches with is_expired=0 surface as 'expiring soon' with negative days
findings.detail: expiringSoon filters b.expiry_date <= :cutoff with no >= today bound. A batch whose expiry_date is already in the past but whose is_expired flag was never flipped to 1 (the flag is set by a separate process/trigger; nothing in this code path maintains it) will match, and InventoryPage renders it in the 'Expiring soon' / overview lists with a negative day count and a blue/orange color. The Days color logic (InventoryPage.cpp:292) only distinguishes <=30 vs not, so a -40 day row is shown identically to a 25-day row. PHP's stock.php derives status purely from (expiry_date - CURRENT_DATE) and flags days<=0 as EXPIRED, so a past-date row there reads EXPIRED, not 'expiring soon'.
findings.recommendation: Add AND b.expiry_date >= date('now') to expiringSoon (and/or treat days<=0 as expired in the rendering), so already-lapsed batches don't masquerade as upcoming-expiry stock.

findings.title: Badge/qty colors are hardcoded hex values that drift from the theme tokens (violates the single-source-of-truth rule)
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md states design tokens in resources/theme.qss are the single source of truth and 'don't hardcode colors elsewhere.' InventoryPage hardcodes #dc2828 (danger), #db7706 (warning), #0da2e7 (info), #607085 (neutral), #279b74 (success) for the status ladder, and AdjustmentsPage.cpp:337 hardcodes the same red/green. These don't even match the app.css tokens: --destructive resolves to ~#e02424 (theme.qss button uses #e02424) but the status text uses #dc2828; --success is 160 60% 38% (~#279c6c) vs #279b74; --warning is 32 95% 44% (~#d97706) vs #db7706. The result is two slightly different palettes for the same semantic colors.
findings.recommendation: Centralize semantic colors (danger/warning/info/neutral/success) in one C++ helper that reads from the theme palette, and reuse it in InventoryPage and AdjustmentsPage so they cannot drift from theme.qss / app.css.

findings.title: StockInDialog allows cost or MRP of 0.00 and an MRP below cost without warning
findings.detail: Validation only rejects empty or negative cost/MRP (isNegative()), so a zero cost or zero MRP passes. A zero cost silently zeroes the blended-cost weighting and the stock-at-cost KPI; a zero/below-cost MRP means the item sells at or below cost. The dialog also doesn't surface whether the GRN/blended-cost recompute happened. Confirm against Grn.php/StockInDraft handling whether zero is permitted on receive; if PHP rejects or warns on MRP<cost, the Qt dialog should match.
findings.recommendation: Compare against the PHP receive/GRN path: if zero cost/MRP or MRP<cost is disallowed or warned there, add the same guard here; otherwise document that zero is intentionally accepted.

findings.title: GRN notes field is dropped — port-parity regression
findings.detail: The PHP grn-edit.php form has a 'Notes (optional)' textarea (lines 166-169) that is passed into Grn::post() and stored on grn_documents.notes, and the read-only PHP view renders it back (lines 463-468). GrnService::post() in Qt accepts a notes argument (GrnService.h:41) and the SQL inserts the column, but GrnDialog never builds a notes widget and always calls post() with the default empty QString. Operators therefore cannot record delivery remarks (damaged box, short shipment, etc.) that the source-of-truth app captures, and GrnDetailDialog has no place to show them.
findings.recommendation: Add a multi-line QPlainTextEdit 'Notes (optional)' to GrnDialog's form, trim it, and pass it as the notes argument to service.post(). Render notes in GrnDetailDialog::load() when non-empty, mirroring grn-edit.php lines 463-468.

findings.title: Detail view omits supplier context strip shown by PHP
findings.detail: grn-edit.php renders a supplier context strip (name, phone, payment terms, NTN, salesman) on every GRN view, in both DRAFT and POSTED states (lines 116-140). GrnDetailDialog::loadHeader only selects suppliers.name and the meta line shows only supplier name + invoice + posted + status. The phone/terms/NTN/salesman context an operator uses to reconcile a delivery against the supplier is missing.
findings.recommendation: Extend loadHeader's JOIN to pull s.contact_phone, s.payment_terms, s.ntn, s.salesman_name and render them in the meta block (or a small grid) like the PHP card body.

findings.title: No DRAFT/CANCELLED lifecycle — GRN is post-only, irreversible with no undo path
findings.detail: PHP models a full GRN lifecycle: createDraft -> post -> cancelDraft (Grn.php:27-310), and grn-edit.php renders an editable DRAFT vs a read-only POSTED view, with the badge supporting DRAFT/POSTED/CANCELLED. The Qt port collapses this to a single modal that posts immediately; PurchasingPage.reloadGrns() even color-codes a CANCELLED status (PurchasingPage.cpp:199) that the UI can never produce. There is no way to save a partially-entered GRN, no draft recovery if the operator closes mid-entry, and no cancel action. Since posting is irreversible (creates batches + inventory_movements), the absence of any draft/cancel safety net is a meaningful operational gap versus the spec.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) document this as an intentional simplification in CLAUDE.md/MEMORY port-gaps, or (b) reintroduce draft persistence and a cancel action. At minimum, drop the dead CANCELLED color-coding or wire a cancel path so the status set the UI displays matches what it can create.

findings.title: Expiry editor has no minimumDate; relies solely on post-hoc validation
findings.detail: m_expiry is a QDateEdit defaulted to today+1y but with no setMinimumDate(QDate::currentDate()). The user can scroll/type a past expiry and only learns it is invalid after pressing Add (accept() line 216). The calendar popup also lets the operator pick clearly invalid past months. The HTML date input in PHP behaves similarly, but a native control should prevent the obviously-invalid selection up front for a fast data-entry screen.
findings.recommendation: Call m_expiry->setMinimumDate(QDate::currentDate()) so past dates cannot be entered, keeping the accept() check as a backstop.

findings.title: Duplicate medicine+batch+expiry lines silently merge with no UI feedback
findings.detail: addLine() unconditionally appends whatever GrnLineDialog returns. If an operator adds two lines for the same medicine+batch#+expiry (easy to do by re-scanning), the GrnDialog table shows two distinct rows and two line totals, but GrnService's find-or-create keys on (medicine,batch,expiry) and merges them into one batch. The subtotal stays correct and the ledger stays consistent, but the receipt the operator reviewed (two rows) does not match the single merged batch row, which is confusing during a delivery reconciliation. PHP has the same find-or-create merge but at least keeps separate grn_lines rows; the difference here is the UI gives no hint a merge will occur.
findings.recommendation: On addLine(), detect an existing line with the same medicineId+batchNumber+expiry and either offer to combine quantities or warn the operator before appending a second visually-identical row.

findings.title: No active suppliers is a soft dead-end inside the GRN dialog
findings.detail: If there are no active suppliers, the combobox is disabled and shows '(add a supplier first)', but the dialog still opens fully and lets the operator enter lines before postGrn() finally rejects with 'Choose a supplier.' (line 165). The operator can waste effort filling lines that can never post. There is no shortcut to add a supplier from here, unlike the Suppliers tab.
findings.recommendation: When m_supplier->count()==0, either block newGrn() in PurchasingPage with a message ('Add a supplier first') and an offer to open SupplierDialog, or disable Add line / Post and surface guidance prominently.

findings.title: Detail dialog (and GRN list) not refreshed/anchored to lifecycle; opening detail does not reload list
findings.detail: openGrn() opens a read-only GrnDetailDialog and never reloads the list afterward; combined with the post-only design this is currently harmless, but if a cancel/edit path is ever added it will leave stale rows. Also note the only way to view a GRN is double-click; there is no explicit 'View'/'Open' button next to 'New GRN', which is a discoverability gap relative to the rest of the page's button-driven affordances.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit 'Open' button for the selected GRN, and reloadGrns() after any dialog that can mutate a GRN. Low priority while GRNs are immutable post-post.

findings.title: No tests cover the dialog-level validation/preview logic
findings.detail: grn_tests.cpp thoroughly covers GrnService.post() (subtotal, blended cost, FOC dilution, dup-batch merge, all rejection paths). But GrnLineDialog::accept() re-implements the same validation rules (batch required, expiry-not-past, cost>0, MRP>0 — lines 213-224) and GrnLineDialog::updatePreview()/GrnDialog::renderLines() re-implement subtotal and blended-cost display via CostBlender. None of this UI-side duplicated logic is tested, so a drift between the dialog's pre-check and the service's authoritative check (e.g. different zero/negative handling, the regex validator vs Money::compare) could ship undetected. The CLAUDE.md guardrail requires tests on money/stock/expiry paths, and the dialog is on that path.
findings.recommendation: Add focused tests for the GRN line preview/validation: assert GrnLineDialog accept() rejects the same cases the service rejects, and that renderLines()/updatePreview() subtotal and blended-cost strings match CostBlender output for representative inputs (paid-only, FOC dilution, multi-line).

findings.title: CSV injection guard from PHP Csv.php is missing in all Qt exports
findings.detail: PHP's Csv::writeRow deliberately prefixes any cell whose first char is one of = + - @ \t \r with a single quote to stop Excel/Calc from evaluating it as a formula (the PHP comment explicitly calls out 'pop calc.exe on the accountant's machine' via a planted brand_name/customer_name). The Qt CSV writers (csvField in AnalyticsRepository and the field lambda in SalesReportRepository::exportCsv) only RFC-4180 quote commas/quotes/newlines and do NOT apply the formula-injection prefix. Brand names, generic names, patient names, cashier names, etc. flow straight into the exported CSV, so a value like '=cmd|...' or '-2+3' in a medicine/customer field is emitted unescaped. This is a regression of a security control that exists in the source-of-truth app.
findings.recommendation: Add the formula-leading-char guard (prefix with a single quote when field[0] is in "=+-@\t\r") to a single shared CSV-cell helper and use it from every exporter, matching Csv.php exactly.

findings.title: CSV export dropped from Tax, Refunds, Compliance, Narcotic register, and Velocity reports
findings.detail: Only ReportsPage (Sales), TopSellersWidget, and PlReportWidget have an Export CSV button. The PHP equivalents for tax.php, refunds.php, compliance.php, narcotic-register.php, and velocity.php all expose a CSV download (Csv::stream). Narcotic register is a DRAP regulatory document where CSV export for inspectors is a real workflow; losing it is a parity and compliance gap, not cosmetic. The repository even lacks export functions for these reports (only exportPlCsv / exportTopSellersCsv exist alongside SalesReportRepository::exportCsv).
findings.recommendation: Add Export CSV buttons + repository exporters for tax, refunds, compliance, narcotic, and velocity, with the same column headers/order as the PHP Csv::stream calls.

findings.title: Exported CSVs lack the UTF-8 BOM and CRLF line endings that PHP emits
findings.detail: PHP Csv::stream writes a UTF-8 BOM (\xEF\xBB\xBF) so Excel opens the file with the PKR/UTF-8 glyphs intact, and terminates every row with CRLF (\r\n) per RFC 4180. The Qt QTextStream exporters write UTF-8 without a BOM and end rows with '\n'. The headers also embed 'PKR' in column titles but values are bare numbers in PHP; here the row money values are bare numbers too, so opening in Excel on a non-UTF-8 locale can mangle any non-ASCII characters in medicine/patient names. This diverges from the documented intent of the source CSV writer.
findings.recommendation: Set QTextStream encoding to UTF-8 with setGenerateByteOrderMark(true) (or write the BOM bytes manually) and emit '\r\n' line endings to match Csv.php.

findings.title: Narcotic register 'Items' uses wrong separator vs PHP (', ' instead of '; ')
findings.detail: PHP narcotic-register.php joins items with STRING_AGG(..., '; ') (semicolon-space). The Qt narcoticRegister query uses GROUP_CONCAT(..., ', ') (comma-space). For a DRAP register where each line is 'Brand × qty unit', a comma separator is ambiguous when a brand/unit itself contains a comma, and it visibly differs from the regulatory document the PHP app produces. (Compliance correctly uses ', ' to match its PHP page, so the two are simply inconsistent with their respective sources.)
findings.recommendation: Change the narcotic GROUP_CONCAT separator to '; ' to match narcotic-register.php.

findings.title: Compliance 'Items' set and format diverge from PHP (bracketed schedule, controlled-only join, no LIMIT)
findings.detail: PHP compliance.php joins ALL sale_items (no controlled filter on the joined medicine), filters rows with (has_controlled_drug = TRUE OR m.controlled_schedule <> 'NONE'), aggregates items as 'brand (SCHEDULE)' with parentheses, and caps results at LIMIT 500. The Qt query (a) restricts the item join to m.controlled_schedule <> 'NONE', so the Items column only ever lists controlled lines (a non-controlled line on a controlled sale is hidden), (b) formats as 'brand [SCHEDULE]' with square brackets instead of parentheses, and (c) has no LIMIT 500. The row-inclusion predicate is also reworked into an EXISTS subquery; while likely equivalent, it is not a literal port and changes the displayed Items content.
findings.recommendation: Mirror compliance.php: aggregate items over all joined lines surviving the WHERE, use 'brand (SCHEDULE)' parentheses, and add LIMIT 500. Add a test comparing the Items string against a PHP fixture.

findings.title: 'When' / 'Witness at' columns show UTC while filtering is done in local time
findings.detail: sold_at is stored via SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (UTC, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS') — see SaleService.cpp:217. Every date filter correctly converts with date(sold_at,'localtime'), but the tables display the raw UTC sold_at string verbatim. A late-night local sale is filtered into its local date yet shown with a UTC clock time (and possibly a different calendar date), so the displayed timestamp can contradict the day the user filtered on. PHP stored TIMESTAMPTZ and rendered in the session timezone, so its display matched the filter. This affects Sales, Compliance, Narcotic 'When' and Narcotic 'Witness at'.
findings.recommendation: Convert sold_at/narcotic_witness_at to localtime for display (e.g. SELECT datetime(sold_at,'localtime') or format in C++) so the shown time matches the localtime-based filtering, and truncate to 19 chars like PHP's substr(...,0,19).

findings.title: Report money/percentage outputs are not pinned bit-for-bit against PHP in tests
findings.detail: The CLAUDE.md guardrails require pricing/money paths to match PHP bit-for-bit AND be covered by tests. The analytics tests are existence/smoke checks: tax only asserts 'tax report produces a total' (!tx.total.isEmpty()), compliance/narcotic assert 'runs (size=N)' and 'at least one row', and there are no assertions fixing the exact values of marginPct, sharePct, the inclusive tax base/tax split (the ratioMul rounding in AnalyticsRepository.cpp:25-53), or the refund-proportional COGS reduction (cogsNet = cogs − refunds×cogs/revenue). These are precisely the HALF_UP-at-scale-4 computations most likely to drift from PHP. A regression in the rounding would pass the current suite.
findings.recommendation: Add value-asserting cases that seed a known sale+refund and check margin%, share%, refund-proportional COGS, and inclusive/exclusive tax base/tax against numbers computed by the PHP pages, not just non-emptiness.

findings.title: Velocity widget claims 'net units' but query never subtracts returns; no date filter
findings.detail: The velocity table description says 'counts are net units sold', but velocityReport() sums si.qty_in_base_units over non-voided sales and never deducts returned units, so the figures are gross, not net. The label is misleading to a pharmacist reconciling movement. (The PHP velocity.php is also rolling-window/all-time with no date inputs, so the missing date filter is acceptable parity, but the 'net' wording is a Qt-side inaccuracy.)
findings.recommendation: Either reword the description to 'units sold' (gross) or net out returns to match the wording; pick one consistently with the PHP page.

findings.title: Settings changes are not audited (PHP records SETTINGS_UPDATED, Qt does not)
findings.detail: PHP admin/settings.php calls Audit::write($adminId,'SETTINGS_UPDATED','settings',...) on every branding save and theme change. The Qt savePharmacy(), savePrinter(), and saveBackupSettings() slots call SettingsRepository::set() (a bare UPSERT with no audit) and never write an audit row. The codebase already has Audit::write (src/data/Audit.h) wired into users, suppliers, sales, GRN, stock adjustments, sessions, etc., so this is an omission, not a missing capability. Pharmacy name/NTN/return-policy/theme/printer-queue/backup-folder changes are therefore invisible in the append-only audit trail that the CLAUDE.md guardrails require for who-did-what-when on admin actions.
findings.recommendation: After a successful set() batch in savePharmacy/savePrinter/saveBackupSettings, call Audit::write(m_db, m_user.id, "SETTINGS_UPDATED", "settings", 0, ...) (entity null/0 as in PHP). Ideally do it inside the same transaction as the writes (see next finding).

findings.title: Multi-key settings writes are not transactional (partial-update on failure)
findings.detail: savePharmacy() issues 8 separate SettingsRepository::set() UPSERTs (name, address, phone, ntn, policy, footer, theme, logo_path) with no surrounding transaction; savePrinter() and saveBackupSettings() do 2 each. SettingsRepository::setMany() also just loops set() with no BEGIN/COMMIT. CLAUDE.md mandates wrapping every multi-statement change in a transaction. If one set() fails midway (disk full, locked DB), the config is left half-applied and the user still sees the success message that follows. The page also calls Theme::apply() and shows 'Settings saved.' unconditionally, ignoring the bool return of every set() — a failed write is reported as success.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each save in QSqlDatabase::transaction()/commit() (rollback on first failed set()), check the boolean results, and only show the success QMessageBox + apply the theme when the commit succeeds; otherwise show set()'s error.

findings.title: Address and return-policy fields enforce no length limit (PHP caps 500/2000)
findings.detail: PHP settings.php enforces server-side $LIMITS (address 500, return_policy_text 2000) and rejects over-length input. In Qt the QLineEdit fields use setMaxLength to mirror the limits, but m_phAddress and m_phPolicy are QPlainTextEdit with NO maxlength and savePharmacy() does no length check before persisting. The matching constants (MaxPharmacyAddress=500, MaxReturnPolicy=2000) already exist in SettingsKeys.h but are unused here. An operator can save an arbitrarily long address/policy that diverges from PHP-validated data and may overflow the receipt layout.
findings.recommendation: In savePharmacy(), validate trimmed length of m_phAddress (<=500) and m_phPolicy (<=2000) using the existing SettingsKeys constants and show a warning + abort if exceeded, matching the PHP error path; optionally connect QPlainTextEdit::textChanged to truncate.

findings.title: CUPS status re-probed via blocking QProcess on every keystroke in the queue combo
findings.detail: m_thermalQueue (an editable QComboBox) is connected to AdminPage::refreshPrinterStatus via currentTextChanged. refreshPrinterStatus() calls CupsStatus::snapshot() and CupsStatus::usbPrinters(), which run multiple synchronous QProcess invocations (lpstat -r, queue lookup, lpinfo for USB) on the GUI thread, each with waitForFinished timeouts up to 2000ms (CupsStatus.cpp:20-36,49). Typing a custom queue name therefore spawns several blocking subprocesses per character, and if CUPS is down each call burns its full timeout, freezing the UI for seconds. PHP only probes on page load / POST, not per keystroke.
findings.recommendation: Debounce the currentTextChanged handler (e.g. a 400ms single-shot QTimer) or only re-probe on combo activation/editingFinished, not on every text change; consider running CUPS probes off the GUI thread (QtConcurrent) and updating labels via signal.

findings.title: set()/Theme::apply() return values ignored; failures reported as success
findings.detail: savePharmacy(), savePrinter(), and backupNow()'s LastBackupAt write all ignore the bool returned by SettingsRepository::set() and unconditionally pop an information() 'saved' dialog. A locked or read-only DB silently drops the change while telling the user it was saved. Theme::apply() reads the QSS resource and also has no failure surface. Combined with the non-transactional writes above, an operator can believe a critical config (e.g. printer queue, backup folder) is persisted when it is not.
findings.recommendation: Check the boolean from each set() (SettingsRepository already records m_error) and only show the success dialog when all writes succeed; otherwise surface SettingsRepository::error().

findings.title: No unit tests for AdminPage save/validation logic
findings.detail: The only AdminPage coverage is screenshots.cpp (renders the page for visual capture) and a smoke.cpp settings upsert/read round-trip on SettingsRepository directly. There are no tests for the admin-facing behaviors: required-name validation, length caps, theme persistence, printer enable/queue persistence, backup-folder gating in backupNow(), or the (currently missing) SETTINGS_UPDATED audit emission. CLAUDE.md does not class settings on the money/stock/expiry critical path, so this is low, but the validation parity with PHP is untested and easy to regress.
findings.recommendation: Add a small test exercising a SettingsService/save path: required name rejected, over-length address/policy rejected, theme round-trips, and (after fixing) that a SETTINGS_UPDATED audit row is written. Extract the validation out of the slot into a testable helper if needed.

findings.title: Backup-tab actions and Change-my-PIN not widget-gated (relies solely on nav hiding)
findings.detail: Most editors gate on m_isAdmin (lines 192,213-216,271,314-315,347-348), but the Backup tab's Choose-folder / Back-up-now / Save / auto-backup checkbox and the top 'Change my PIN' button are always enabled. Access control currently depends entirely on MainWindow only adding the Admin nav action when isAdmin (MainWindow.cpp:168). The AdminPage object is, however, always constructed (MainWindow.cpp:47) for every role, so if a future nav/keyboard-shortcut change exposed it to a MANAGER, backup and DB-file export would be reachable. Change-my-PIN being enabled for any user is correct; the backup actions are not gated as defense-in-depth.
findings.recommendation: Gate the backup action buttons + auto-backup checkbox on m_isAdmin (matching the rest of the page), or skip constructing/registering AdminPage entirely for non-admins. Treat nav-hiding as cosmetic, not the access boundary.

findings.title: Logo file is copied to disk before Save, leaving an orphaned file if the user cancels
findings.detail: changeLogo() immediately copies the chosen image to AppPaths::logosDir()/logo.<ext> and removes any prior file, updating m_logoPath in memory. The logo_path setting is only persisted later in savePharmacy(). If the operator changes the logo then closes the page without saving, the on-disk logo has already been overwritten while the stored setting still points at the old path (now deleted) — the preview/receipt logo can break until a Save. Minor, single-PC, but the side effect on the filesystem happens out of step with the explicit Save action used for every other field on the tab.
findings.recommendation: Either persist logo_path immediately on copy (it's a file the user explicitly picked) or stage the copy to a temp name and only move it into place on Save; at minimum keep the previous logo file until Save succeeds.

findings.title: Z-report sales recap omits refund netting that PHP performs
findings.detail: loadRecap() sums grand_total over the session's sales into cash/card/all totals and never subtracts refunds. The PHP source-of-truth ZReport::buildPayload() (../pos/backend/services/ZReport.php:160-188) queries the returns table for refunds processed during the shift by the session's cashier, splits them by the original sale's payment mode, and subtracts: cashTotal -= refundsCash, cardTotal -= refundsCard, allTotal -= refundsAll. The PHP z-report.php even renders the heading 'Sales recap (net of refunds)' and a whole 'Refunds during shift' block (refund_count, refunds_cash, refunds_card, refunds_total). The Qt Z-report therefore overstates cash/card/grand totals for any shift in which a return was processed, and entirely drops the refunds section. This is a money-path divergence on a regulator-facing document.
findings.recommendation: Port the refund query and net the recap exactly as PHP does (join returns on original_sale_id, filter to created_at within the session window and initiated_by = cashier_id, split by payment mode), subtract from cash/card/all via Money, and add a 'Refunds during shift' section when refund_count>0. Cover with a test that sells then returns within a shift and asserts the recap matches PHP-equivalent net figures.

findings.title: 'My shift' recent list shows and opens other cashiers' shifts (port-parity / IDOR)
findings.detail: reload() populates the 'My shift' Recent-sessions table from SessionRepository::list(50), which is global across all cashiers (header at SessionRepository.h:69 says 'across all cashiers (admin view)'). The PHP /pos/session page scopes recent shifts to 'WHERE s.cashier_id = :c' (../pos/frontend/pages/pos/session.php:55) for the cashier view, and z-report.php enforces an IDOR guard (../pos/frontend/pages/sessions/z-report.php:46-57) so a non-manager cannot view another cashier's Z-report. In the Qt port, showZReport() opens ZReportDialog for any selected row with no role/ownership check, so a plain CASHIER can read any other cashier's takings, variance, and signed Z-report from the 'My shift' tab.
findings.recommendation: Filter the 'My shift' table to the logged-in cashier (add a cashier-scoped query/overload), and gate showZReport() so non-manager/admin users can only open their own sessions' Z-reports. Reserve the unfiltered list() for the manager-only Reconcile tab.

findings.title: Z-report HMAC payload/scheme not compatible with PHP and signs raw stored fields, not the computed recap
findings.detail: canonicalPayload() builds a pipe-joined string of raw cashier_sessions columns (session_id, cashier_id, timestamps, floats, status). PHP signs a ksorted JSON object of the COMPUTED recap including cash/card/all totals, refund breakdown, sale_receipts, etc. (../pos/backend/services/ZReport.php:195-235). CLAUDE.md permits simplifying the HMAC chain for single-PC, so non-bit-compatibility is acceptable, but the Qt signature covers neither the recap totals nor the receipt list, so tampering with a sale's grand_total or deleting a sale would NOT invalidate the Qt signature — undermining the 'tamper-evident' claim printed on the report (ZReportDialog.cpp:208). It also signs raw DB strings whose exact formatting (e.g. counted_cash '' vs '0.00') can drift, risking unstable signatures.
findings.recommendation: Include the computed recap (cash/card/all totals, refund totals, receipt numbers) in the signed payload so the signature actually detects sales tampering, and normalize numeric fields through Money before signing for stability. Document explicitly that this is a single-PC simplification of the PHP chain.

findings.title: Close-shift flow drops the optional notes captured by PHP
findings.detail: PHP's close form posts an optional 'notes' textarea and Sessions::close() persists it (notes = COALESCE(:notes, notes)) — see session.php:166-169 and Sessions.php:79,132. The Qt close flow uses a single QInputDialog for counted cash only; SessionRepository::closeSession() takes no notes parameter and never writes the notes column. End-of-day annotations (e.g. 'till jam, recounted twice') are silently lost, reducing the audit value of a CLOSED shift.
findings.recommendation: Replace the single-field QInputDialog with a small dialog that captures counted cash + optional notes, add a notes parameter to closeSession(), and write it with COALESCE semantics matching PHP.

findings.title: No tests for ZReportDialog recap, refund netting, or signature stability
findings.detail: sessions_tests.cpp covers SessionRepository open/close/bump/expected-variance and Reconciler thoroughly, but there is zero coverage of the Z-report money path: ZReportDialog::loadRecap cash/card/all tallies, the (currently missing) refund netting, and ZReportArchive::signAndStore idempotency/tamper-detection. CLAUDE.md mandates tests on the money and the Z-report tamper-evidence paths. The refund-netting bug above would have been caught by such a test.
findings.recommendation: Add tests that build a session with mixed CASH/CARD sales plus a return, assert the recap totals (net of refunds) match expected Money values bit-for-bit, and assert signAndStore returns the same signature on re-view (idempotent) and that the archive row is append-only.

findings.title: computeSignature/signAndStore not wrapped in a transaction and signer userId hardcoded to 0
findings.detail: signAndStore() does a SELECT-then-INSERT OR IGNORE without a surrounding transaction; on the first view of a freshly-closed shift two near-simultaneous opens of the dialog could both miss the existing row and race the insert (mitigated only by the UNIQUE/IGNORE, but the returned res.signatureHex from the loser path is the freshly computed one, not necessarily the stored one). More importantly, ZReportDialog::computeSignature constructs ZReportArchive(m_db, 0) (comment at line 104: 'No current-user id is plumbed into this dialog; the signer accepts 0'), so generated_by is always NULL — the audit/provenance of who generated the Z-report is lost, whereas PHP records generatedBy (ZReport::generate's $generatedBy). The dialog is constructed with no userId at all.
findings.recommendation: Plumb the current userId into ZReportDialog and on to ZReportArchive so generated_by is recorded. Wrap the read-existing/insert in a transaction (or rely on an INSERT ... RETURNING / re-SELECT after IGNORE) so the returned signature is always the persisted one.

findings.title: Close generates Z-report on a stale session id without checking close succeeded against reload
findings.detail: closeShift() computes variance for the confirmation prompt using sessionSummary() read before the confirm, then calls closeSession(); the counted-cash string passed to Money::fromString at line 395 is the raw dialog text, but closeSession re-validates via isMoneyInput and will fail later for non-numeric input — yet the user already saw a 'balanced/short/over' message computed from a possibly-invalid Money::fromString(text) (which silently parses garbage as 0). So an entry like 'abc' shows 'short by PKR <expected>' in the confirm dialog, then the close is rejected with a different message. Minor UX/correctness mismatch versus PHP which validates the pattern up front.
findings.recommendation: Validate the counted-cash input against the same ^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$ pattern before showing the variance confirmation, so the preview and the eventual accept/reject are consistent.
