findings.title: Variance color thresholds and rounding could mis-signal on tiny residuals
findings.detail: Variance coloring uses Money::isNegative()/isZero() on the stored scale-2 variance, which is correct, but the close-time preview at line 397 uses variance.isZero() on a value derived from Money::fromString(text) that may carry >2 dp if the user types e.g. '1080.005' (isMoneyInput only later rejects >2dp on commit). The preview can therefore label a 3-dp entry 'balanced' while the committed counted value is rounded differently. Low impact given the pattern rejects >2dp at commit, but the preview is computed before that rejection.
findings.recommendation: Round/validate the preview value to scale-2 (or reject >2dp) before computing the displayed variance so the preview matches the stored result.

findings.title: Cashier can process a full refund with no manager authorization (segregation-of-duties bypass)
findings.detail: processReturn() only prompts for credentials when ControlledSubstancePolicy::requiresWitness(schedule) is true (NARCOTIC only). For every ordinary medicine, a logged-in CASHIER refunds cash and disposes of stock (RESTOCK or WRITE_OFF) in a single click with zero second-person check. The PHP source (pos/frontend/pages/pos/returns/initiate.php) requires, for a non-manager operator, a ManagerOverride::verify(...,'return_initiate') PIN belonging to a DIFFERENT user before Returns::initiate is ever called — explicit segregation of duties on a cash-out / stock-mutating path. The Qt port drops this entirely. ReturnService::commitReturn sets authorized_by = m_userId (the cashier themself), so the audit row also records no independent authorizer.
findings.recommendation: Before calling commitReturn for a non-manager user, gate the refund behind a ManagerOverrideDialog and UserRepository::verifyManagerOverride with a 'return_initiate' purpose, requiring a manager/admin whose id != m_userId; pass that id through as the authorizing manager (separate from the narcotic witness). Mirror the PHP rule that MANAGER/ADMIN operators self-authorize.

findings.title: Returns workflow collapsed: no PENDING_REVIEW / manager adjudication step on the operator path
findings.detail: PHP Returns::initiate creates a PENDING_REVIEW row with a RETURN_QUARANTINE movement (current_qty unchanged — stock held pending QA) and a manager later adjudicates at /admin/returns. The Qt Process-return tab instead calls ReturnService::commitReturn, which immediately writes a final status (APPROVED_RESTOCK or WRITE_OFF), mutates batches.current_qty, and recomputes the sale status — skipping the quarantine/review gate the PHP app enforces. The 'Review queue' tab and ReturnService::initiate/adjudicate exist but are unreachable from the operator flow, so the only way returns reach review is never exercised by this UI. This means a cashier's restock decision is never QA-reviewed, contradicting the documented PHP state machine (RETURN_QUARANTINE -> adjudicate).
findings.recommendation: Decide intentionally: either route the operator action through initiate() (PENDING_REVIEW + quarantine) so the Review queue is the single adjudication point matching PHP, or document/justify the immediate-disposition model with the user. If kept, restrict immediate WRITE_OFF/RESTOCK by a cashier (it currently lets them both refund and dispose of stock unreviewed).

findings.title: "Void sale" is a net-new destructive feature with no authorization gate and no PHP equivalent
findings.detail: The Void-sale button restocks every line of a COMPLETED sale and marks it VOIDED via ReturnService::voidSale, behind only a yes/no confirmation. There is no manager-override or witness check, and it is on the 'Process return' tab visible to all roles including CASHIER. grep of pos/frontend/routes.php and pos/backend confirms the PHP app has NO void-sale route or Sale void method at all — this is a feature invented in the port. A full sale reversal (cash + all stock) is the most privileged operation in the module and is currently the least guarded.
findings.recommendation: Either remove it (to match PHP) or, at minimum, gate it behind a manager-override PIN (id != operator), confirm against same-day-only or a documented policy, and hide the button for cashiers. ReturnService::voidSale already accepts sameDayOnly but the UI hardcodes false (line 595).

findings.title: voidSale called with sameDayOnly=false — no time/role constraint on full reversal
findings.detail: ReturnService::voidSale supports a sameDayOnly guard, but ReturnsPage passes false unconditionally, so any historical COMPLETED sale can be voided in full at any later date by anyone with the page open. Combined with the lack of an authorization gate (finding above), an old high-value receipt can be reversed with two clicks. Even if void is retained, unbounded back-dated reversal is a cash-control risk.
findings.recommendation: Pass sameDayOnly=true unless a manager override is provided, mirroring the cash-control intent; surface a clear message when a non-same-day sale is rejected (the service already returns one).

findings.title: No UI-level tests for the returns screen flows
findings.detail: Returns tests cover the service layer only. There is no coverage asserting the UI's authorization branching (controlled vs non-controlled, witness == operator rejection), the enable/disable logic for m_processBtn / m_voidBtn / m_markSentBtn, the qty spinbox clamping to 'remaining' on selection change, or that the supplier 'Mark sent' button only enables for unsettled rows. Given CLAUDE.md mandates tests on quantity/stock/refund paths, the witness-required and remaining-qty guards in this file are untested at the UI boundary.
findings.recommendation: Add a QtTest fixture that constructs ReturnsPage against an in-memory seeded DB and asserts: controlled line forces the witness dialog; selecting a fully-returned line disables Refund and clamps qty to 1; a CASHIER role hides the Review queue/Supplier tabs; Mark-sent stays disabled for settled rows.

findings.title: Reason and Restock inputs are not reset after a successful refund, risking carry-over mistakes
findings.detail: After a successful return, only m_condition is cleared and lookup() re-runs. m_reason keeps the previously chosen reason and m_restock keeps its prior checked state. Because the form sits directly above the (refreshed) sale lines, an operator processing several lines of the same receipt can silently inherit the wrong reason/disposition for the next line. The PHP page renders an independent per-line form each request, so there is no sticky carry-over.
findings.recommendation: After a successful refund reset m_reason to its first item and m_restock to checked (the documented default), and clear the line selection so the operator must re-pick deliberately.

findings.title: Recent-returns status badges lose the plain-English captions present in the PHP UI
findings.detail: PHP /pos/returns/history maps each status to a human label plus a tooltip caption explaining the stock effect (e.g. PENDING_REVIEW = 'Cash refunded — stock held in quarantine until a manager adjudicates'; APPROVED_RESTOCK explains qty_in_stock increased by N). The Qt recent table only colors the raw enum text (APPROVED_RESTOCK / WRITE_OFF / PENDING_REVIEW) with no tooltip and no handling for RETURN_TO_SUPPLIER, so operators lose the at-a-glance explanation of what happened to the stock. It also leaves RETURN_TO_SUPPLIER uncolored/uncaptioned.
findings.recommendation: Map each status to a friendly label and set a QTableWidgetItem tooltip mirroring the PHP captions; add the RETURN_TO_SUPPLIER ('info') case.

findings.title: Role lookup and per-line schedule query run raw on the UI thread without error surfacing
findings.detail: The constructor's role query and the controlled-schedule lookup in processReturn() are inlined raw QSqlQuery calls in the view layer, contrary to CLAUDE.md's data-access -> domain -> UI layering (everything else in this page goes through ReturnRepository/ReturnService). If the role query fails (db error), role stays empty and the manager tabs silently vanish with no diagnostic; if the schedule query fails, schedule stays empty and a NARCOTIC line could skip the witness gate without any error shown. Defence-in-depth exists in the service (requireWitnessIfControlled re-checks), so it is not exploitable, but the silent-failure UX and layer leak are maintainability/reliability smells.
findings.recommendation: Move the role lookup and schedule lookup into UserRepository/MedicineRepository (or ReturnRepository) methods that return a typed result, and treat a query failure as a hard error (disable the action / show a message) rather than an empty string that quietly relaxes gating.

findings.title: Lockout model diverges from PHP RateLimit spec with no documented parity decision
findings.detail: PHP Auth/RateLimit (pos/backend/RateLimit.php) is a sliding 15-minute window of 5 attempts with a progressive in-request delay schedule [0,0,0,1000,5000] ms, keyed by BOTH username and client IP, that resets on success. The Qt port instead implements a persistent 5-strike counter on users.failed_attempts with exponential lock backoff (30s,60s,...,900s) stored in users.locked_until. These produce materially different lockout behavior (e.g. PHP unlocks after the 15-min window regardless of strike count; the port keeps incrementing failed_attempts and lengthening the lock indefinitely until a success clears it). CLAUDE.md treats the PHP app as the spec and deviations as bugs unless documented. There is no comment in LoginDialog.cpp or UserRepository.cpp acknowledging this is an intentional single-PC simplification.
findings.recommendation: Either match the PHP window/delay schedule, or add an explicit comment + a note in the port-gaps memory documenting the chosen single-PC lockout model and why it diverges, and add a test asserting the chosen backoff schedule (30/60/120/.../900) so it does not silently drift.

findings.title: Lockout message exposes raw seconds (up to 900s) — poor UX and weak parity
findings.detail: On lockout the dialog shows "Too many attempts. Try again in 900s." Seconds up to 900 is hard to parse (users must divide by 60), and it diverges from the PHP message "Too many attempts. Please try again later." The +1 in secondsLockedOut (UserRepository.cpp:335) also means a just-expired lock can momentarily display 1s.
findings.recommendation: Format the wait as minutes/seconds (e.g. "15 minutes" / "45 seconds") or fall back to the PHP wording. Keep the numeric value only when under a minute.

findings.title: SetupWizard.accept() is non-atomic: settings committed before the admin 'commit point', leaving partial state and orphaned logo files on retry
findings.detail: accept() (1) copies the logo file, (2) writes ALL settings via setMany, then (3) creates the admin user in a separate transaction. If createAdmin fails (line 116), isFirstRun() stays true (no admin), so the wizard re-runs — but the already-persisted settings and the copied logo.* file remain. persistLogo() (line 66) does QFile::remove(dest) before copy, so a re-run overwrites the logo, but if the user removes the logo on the retry the stale file is never cleaned up, and LogoPath was already written pointing at it. The settings write and admin creation are not in a single DB transaction, so a crash between them leaves a half-configured DB that only the (settings-only, no admin) first-run check papers over.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the settings upsert and admin creation in one DB transaction (createAdmin already opens its own; extend it or add a combined commit method). Persist the logo last, only after the DB commit succeeds, and clean up the copied file if the commit fails.

findings.title: No automated coverage of LoginDialog, ChangePinDialog, or forced-rotation flow
findings.detail: auth_tests.cpp covers only the UserRepository lockout primitives (registerFailedLogin/secondsLockedOut/clearFailedLogins). There is no test for: the LoginDialog attempt() sequence (locked-out short-circuit before verify, generic-failure path, clear+touch+record on success), ChangePinDialog.accept() (wrong current PIN, mismatch, history reuse, differs-from-current, successful persist), or the main.cpp forced-rotation trigger (mustRotatePin OR pinAgeDays >= 90 → mandatory dialog → must_rotate_pin cleared). CLAUDE.md mandates tests on the security/PIN paths. setPin's history-trim and must_rotate_pin clearing are security-critical and untested.
findings.recommendation: Add tests driving UserRepository through the change-PIN path (assert pin_history trimmed to 5, must_rotate_pin reset to 0 after a forced rotation, audit row written) and a headless test of LoginDialog::attempt() outcomes, plus a pinAgeDays-based forced-rotation assertion.

findings.title: Failed-login audit and counter increment are two separate writes that can desync
findings.detail: On a failed attempt the dialog calls recordLogin(...false...) (writes a LOGIN_FAILED audit row) and then registerFailedLogin(username) (a separate transaction that increments failed_attempts / sets locked_until). These are independent operations: if registerFailedLogin's transaction fails (rollback path at UserRepository.cpp:387) the audit log still records a failed attempt that did not count toward lockout, and the UI gives no indication. The PHP Auth.attemptLogin performs the rate-limit accounting and the audit write within the same request flow.
findings.recommendation: Fold the failed-login audit write into the same transaction as registerFailedLogin (or at minimum surface a logged warning if the counter update rolls back) so the audit trail and the lockout counter cannot diverge.

findings.title: ChangePinDialog gives no feedback that a forced (mandatory) change cannot be cancelled-out-of safely
findings.detail: In mandatory mode the dialog only shows a notice but still exposes a Cancel button. In main.cpp (line 123) cancelling a mandatory rotation does `continue` back to the login screen, so the user can never reach the app without rotating — correct behavior — but the dialog itself does not communicate that Cancel = sign out, and a user who closes via the window-close [X] also reaches reject(). The PHP version redirects to /account/change-pin on every request and only allows /logout, making the 'you must rotate or log out' contract explicit.
findings.recommendation: In setMandatory(true), relabel Cancel to 'Sign out' (and/or disable the window close button) so the forced-rotation contract is explicit, matching the PHP redirect-or-logout behavior.

findings.title: pinAgeDays/secondsLockedOut rely on julianday('now') assuming UTC storage; mixed CURRENT_TIMESTAMP vs datetime('now') usage is fragile
findings.detail: pinAgeDays computes julianday('now') - julianday(pin_changed_at), and secondsLockedOut compares locked_until > datetime('now'). pin_changed_at is set via CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (UTC in SQLite) and locked_until via datetime('now') (also UTC), so they are currently consistent. However this couples the 90-day rotation and lockout-expiry correctness to every writer using UTC; any future code that stores a localtime timestamp into these columns would silently skew rotation enforcement or unlock timing. There is no test pinning pinAgeDays to a known age.
findings.recommendation: Add a comment asserting the UTC invariant on pin_changed_at/locked_until, and add a test that back-dates pin_changed_at by 91 days and asserts pinAgeDays>=90 (forced rotation fires).

findings.title: Login username/PIN field validators silently swallow disallowed input, hiding why login fails
findings.detail: The username field uses a QRegularExpressionValidator allowing only [A-Za-z0-9._-] and the PIN field only digits. Pasting/typing other characters is silently rejected at the widget level. If a real username in the DB ever contained other characters (the wizard enforces the same set, so unlikely), the user could never type it and would see only the generic 'Invalid username or PIN.' This is consistent with the wizard's allowed set so it is low-risk, but worth noting as a hard constraint on usernames.
findings.recommendation: No change required if the username charset is intentionally fixed; document the allowed-username charset as a product constraint so admin tooling and any future import cannot create unlogin-able accounts.

findings.title: Receipt HTML interpolates medicine names and totals without HTML-escaping
findings.detail: buildHtml() splices l.name, m_pharmacyName, m_sale.receiptNumber and m_sale.paymentMode straight into an HTML string with no toHtmlEscaped(). A medicine brand name containing '&', '<' or '>' (common in pharmacy data, e.g. "Vitamin C & D", "Cap <Forte>") will render incorrectly or truncate the row in the QTextEdit preview, the printed receipt (doc.setHtml in print()), and the saved PDF. CLAUDE.md flags the receipt/pricing path as a critical, must-be-correct area. The plaintext builder at line 33-56 is dead code (Q_UNUSED(r)), so the only output is this unescaped HTML.
findings.recommendation: Run every interpolated string field (name, unitLabel, pharmacyName, receiptNumber, paymentMode) through QString::toHtmlEscaped() before building the row/header HTML. Add a test that renders a sale with an '&' in the brand name and asserts the receipt total/row count is intact.

findings.title: Discount line shown/hidden via fragile string compare to literal "0.00"
findings.detail: Both the (dead) plaintext builder and buildHtml() decide whether to print a Discount line with `sale.discountTotal != "0.00" && !isEmpty()`. discountTotal is a raw money string. On a live sale SaleService writes discount.toString() (scale-2 -> "0.00"), but SaleRepository::load (src/data/SaleRepository.cpp:22) reads discount_total verbatim from SQLite, where the column DEFAULT is '0' (sql/schema_sqlite.sql:158) and any imported/seeded row may hold "0" or "0.0000". For such rows the literal compare is true and the receipt prints a bogus "Discount -0" line on reprint from ReportsPage. EscPosRenderer.cpp:112 already does this correctly with Money::fromString(...).compare(Money()) > 0; the dialog duplicates the logic the fragile way.
findings.recommendation: Replace the string comparison with Money::fromString(m_sale.discountTotal).compare(Money()) > 0 (matching EscPosRenderer) in both the dialog and any other receipt-format site, ideally via a shared helper.

findings.title: ParkedBillsDialog is not scan-safe; a scanner Enter can trigger Resume/Discard
findings.detail: UiUtil::makeScanSafe() (src/ui/UiUtil.cpp:46) exists specifically to stop a barcode scanner's trailing Enter from firing dialog buttons, and is applied in ManagerOverrideDialog, UserDialog and SupplierDialog. ParkedBillsDialog never calls it, yet it lives in the POS workflow and has a destructive Discard button plus a Resume button. A stray Enter from a scanner (or just Enter on the focused list) can fire the default button. ReceiptDialog and AlternativesDialog are also missing makeScanSafe, the same POS context where a scanner is in hand.
findings.recommendation: Call UiUtil::makeScanSafe(this) at the end of the constructor in ParkedBillsDialog, ReceiptDialog and AlternativesDialog (the helper sets autoDefault/default false on all buttons and installs the Enter-advances filter).

findings.title: SupplierDialog's intended default Save button is silently disabled by makeScanSafe
findings.detail: saveButton->setDefault(true) is called at line 57, then UiUtil::makeScanSafe(this) at line 72 iterates every QPushButton and calls setDefault(false)/setAutoDefault(false). Net effect: the dialog ends up with no default button, so pressing Enter from a non-scanner keyboard does nothing, unlike UserDialog/ManagerOverrideDialog whose QDialogButtonBox handling is consistent. Either the setDefault is dead code (misleading to maintainers) or the intent (Enter saves) is broken.
findings.recommendation: Remove the now-ineffective saveButton->setDefault(true), or decide on a deliberate keyboard-affordance policy and apply it uniformly across the form dialogs. Document that makeScanSafe intentionally strips defaults.

findings.title: No automated tests for dialog validation logic
findings.detail: UserDialog::accept() and SupplierDialog::accept() contain non-trivial validation (username regex, PIN policy on create vs optional reset, force-rotate on admin-reset-of-other, supplier name required) that is the UI-side gate, but tests/ contains only barcode, sale, smoke and screenshots — none exercise these accept() paths. Regressions in the username regex, the create-vs-edit PIN branch, or the discount-visibility logic would ship undetected. CLAUDE.md mandates tests on money/stock/expiry paths; the receipt discount-line and qty rendering touch the money path.
findings.recommendation: Add headless dialog tests (QTest) covering: UserDialog create with weak/short PIN rejected, edit with blank PIN keeps current, admin reset of another user sets forceRotate; SupplierDialog empty-name rejected; ReceiptDialog discount-line shown only for non-zero discount across "0", "0.00", "0.0000" inputs.

findings.title: Logo path interpolated into file:// URL without URL-encoding
findings.detail: logoHtml builds "".arg(m_logoPath) directly. A logo path containing spaces, '#', or non-ASCII characters will not resolve as a file URL and the logo silently disappears from the preview/print/PDF. Should use QUrl::fromLocalFile(m_logoPath).toString() and HTML-escape it.
findings.recommendation: Build the src with QUrl::fromLocalFile(m_logoPath).toString() and toHtmlEscaped(); this also fixes the missing escaping noted in the first finding.

findings.title: AlternativesDialog is read-only — loses PHP add-substitute-to-cart affordance
findings.detail: In the PHP app (frontend/pages/api/medicine-alternatives.php + app.js:261-295) each listed alternative reuses the inline Add-to-cart form, so the cashier can add a substitute brand in one click. The Qt port is explicitly read-only (header comment, AlternativesDialog.h:9-12): the cashier must read off the brand and re-search in the POS. This is an intentional simplification but a workflow-parity regression worth tracking. Minor: the Close button connects QDialogButtonBox::rejected to QDialog::accept() (line 64), which works but is semantically inverted (a Close should reject).
findings.recommendation: If accepted as scope, document the deviation in the PHP-vs-Qt gap memory; otherwise add a 'Add to cart' action emitting the selected medicine id back to PosTerminalPage. Also wire Close to QDialog::reject for clarity.

findings.title: ManagerOverrideDialog does no client-side feedback and verify path is not rate-limited
findings.detail: The dialog itself is fine, but the override flow it feeds differs from PHP: PHP ManagerOverride::verify (pos/backend/services/ManagerOverride.php:35-39) rate-limits override attempts per action/IP and audits OVERRIDE_RATE_LIMITED, defeating PIN brute force. The C++ UserRepository::verifyManagerOverride (src/data/UserRepository.cpp:444-492) writes OVERRIDE_GRANTED/DENIED audit rows but has NO rate limiting, so the dialog can be re-opened and PINs guessed without throttling on the single-PC build. Single-PC lowers the risk but the deviation is a security-relevant parity gap on the manager-PIN gate.
findings.recommendation: Add attempt throttling to verifyManagerOverride (e.g. reuse the login-lockout mechanism keyed by action) or, at minimum, a short backoff after N failures from the dialog, matching the PHP RateLimit semantics.

findings.title: Brand primary teal does not match PHP source-of-truth color
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md mandates same palette as the web app and states the PHP brand teal was 'derived from the actual Care Point Health Clinic logo' and 'matches the reference clinical-pharmacy palette exactly': --primary: 174 84% 24%, which resolves to ~#0d6e6e (a desaturated deep teal). The Qt light theme instead uses #0d9488 (Tailwind teal-600) for primary, with hover #0f766e and pressed #0b5e54. These are noticeably brighter/greener than the PHP brand, so the native app reads as a slightly different product color — the exact thing the visual-fidelity section says to avoid. The same drift exists in dark.qss (#16b8a6), which is a defensible dark-mode lift but is anchored to the wrong base hue.
findings.recommendation: Re-derive the QSS primary/hover/pressed/soft from the PHP HSL tokens (#0d6e6e family) so the native brand matches the web app bit-for-feel, or document an explicit, approved deviation in CLAUDE.md. Keep the dark variant a tint of the corrected base.

findings.title: Inter font referenced everywhere but never bundled — falls back to unknown system font on AlmaLinux
findings.file: resources/theme.qss:26; resources/themes/dark.qss:26; no .ttf/.otf in repo (find found none); no QFontDatabase::addApplicationFont call
findings.detail: Both QSS files set font-family: "Inter", "Segoe UI", "Roboto", sans-serif and the PHP design is built entirely on Inter (--font-sans). No Inter font file is shipped in resources, and nothing calls QFontDatabase::addApplicationFont. On the single-PC AlmaLinux 10 target, Inter, Segoe UI, and Roboto are all typically absent, so Qt silently falls back to the platform default sans (e.g. DejaVu/Noto), changing metrics, weight rendering, and the whole typographic feel the design depends on. The web app also sets font-feature-settings (cv11/ss01/ss03) and tabular-nums which Qt won't get for free.
findings.recommendation: Bundle Inter (or Inter Variable) as a Qt resource and register it via QFontDatabase::addApplicationFont at startup before Theme::apply, or pin a font that is guaranteed present on AlmaLinux. Verify on the actual target. Consider enabling tabular numerals on money/qty labels to match the web's font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

findings.title: Semantic status colors hardcoded across ~10 widgets, mismatching the theme tokens (three palettes)
findings.file: src/ui/DashboardPage.cpp:57,60,62; src/ui/InventoryPage.cpp:25-30,250,270,292; src/ui/SessionsPage.cpp:332-342; src/ui/ReturnsPage.cpp:459,626-630; src/ui/PurchasingPage.cpp:198-199; src/ui/AdjustmentsPage.cpp:337-338; src/ui/MedicinesPage.cpp:127-140
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md says theme.qss is the single source of truth and 'don't hardcode colors elsewhere'. In practice success/warning/danger/info are inlined as hex literals in widget code (#279b74 green, #db7706 amber, #0da2e7 info-blue, #dc2828 red). These match NEITHER the PHP HSL tokens (success 160 60% 38% ~#27996b, warning 32 95% 44% ~#db7706, destructive 0 72% 51% ~#e02424, info 199 89% 48% ~#0ea5e9) NOR the QSS header-comment tokens (success #15a34a, danger #e02424). So there are effectively three competing semantic palettes. The red used in widgets (#dc2828) even differs from the QSS danger (#e02424) and the LoginDialog error (#dc2828) — inconsistent within the app.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a small ThemeTokens/Palette accessor (a header of named QColors, or read from QSS via a custom property/object names) and route all colorItem()/setStyleSheet color calls through it. Align the values to the PHP semantic tokens. This also sets up the next finding (theme-awareness).

findings.title: Hardcoded widget colors are not theme-aware — frozen to light palette in dark mode
findings.file: src/ui/UiUtil.cpp:124 (#607085 muted); src/ui/DashboardPage.cpp:35,57-62; src/ui/InventoryPage.cpp:25-30; all colorItem() call sites
findings.detail: Theme::apply supports a Dark theme (dark.qss, app-bg #0d1117, card #161b22, muted #8b96a5). But every color set in C++ (KPI accents, table cell foregrounds, empty-state text, status badges) is a fixed light-theme hex with no branch on the active theme. In dark mode the empty-state muted text uses #607085 on a #161b22 card (low contrast / hard to read), and saturated light-theme greens/reds sit on dark surfaces unadjusted. The dark theme is therefore only half-implemented: chrome adapts, content colors do not.
findings.recommendation: After centralizing tokens (previous finding), resolve them from the active theme key (or from qApp palette/a parsed token table) so widget-painted colors switch with the theme. At minimum fix the empty-state muted color and any contrast-failing pairs.

findings.title: Muted-text 'token mirror' constant doesn't match the actual muted token
findings.detail: The comment claims kMutedText(#607085) is 'Muted text colour matching the theme's muted token', but the light theme.qss muted token is #64748b and the dark one is #8b96a5. #607085 matches neither. So the empty-state text color is subtly off-brand in light mode and wrong in dark mode. This is the documented hazard of mirroring tokens by hand instead of referencing them.
findings.recommendation: Replace the literal with the real muted token value (#64748b) sourced from the centralized palette, theme-resolved.

findings.title: Base body font-size differs from web (13px vs 14px) and headings/spacing scale diverge
findings.file: resources/theme.qss:27 (font-size 13px) vs app.css:75 (body font-size 14px); h1 22px vs app.css h1 1.75rem=28px
findings.detail: The PHP app uses 14px base body text and h1 28px (1.75rem). The QSS uses 13px base and 22px h1, with controls at 12px font and 36px-tall web buttons reduced to padded 16px-min Qt buttons. Some compression is unavoidable for desktop density, but the net effect is a tighter, smaller-typed feel than the web reference. CLAUDE.md asks to nail palette and component styling first and chase spacing where it matters; the typographic scale is a feel-level deviation worth a conscious decision rather than drift.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the intended desktop type scale against the web app on the target display and document it, or bump base to 14px to match. Low priority vs. color/font findings.

findings.title: Inline HTML in receipt/Z-report uses raw grays outside the token system
findings.detail: Printed/HTML fragments hardcode #444, #666, #e0e5eb etc. These bypass theme tokens entirely. For print this is mostly fine (print is light), but it's another place colors live outside the single source of truth, and the on-screen previews of these dialogs won't follow the dark theme. The PHP @media print rules also map text to the foreground token rather than fixed grays.
findings.recommendation: Move these to the centralized palette (or a dedicated print stylesheet constant) so print styling is intentional and on-screen previews respect the theme.

findings.title: No test covers theme loading or token integrity
findings.detail: Theme::apply silently no-ops if the QSS resource fails to open (the if(open) has no else/log), and there is no test asserting that :/theme.qss and :/themes/dark.qss load non-empty, or that the documented token hexes in the header comments actually appear in the rules. A broken qrc path or a renamed resource would ship an unstyled app with no failing test. Given the project's emphasis on tests for critical paths, the theme is a reasonable smoke-test target.
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight QtTest that calls Theme::apply for "" and "dark", asserts qApp->styleSheet() is non-empty, and optionally checks a couple of anchor tokens (e.g. primary hex) are present. Log a warning when the QSS fails to open.

findings.title: AdminPage (and all manager-only pages) are built and query the DB for every login, including cashiers
findings.detail: MainWindow's constructor unconditionally instantiates all nine pages — DashboardPage, PosTerminalPage, MedicinesPage, InventoryPage, PurchasingPage, ReportsPage, ReturnsPage, SessionsPage, AdminPage — before any role check (lines 39-47). AdminPage's constructor calls reload() (AdminPage.cpp:487), which runs reloadUsers() and reloadAudit(), i.e. it SELECTs the full user list and audit_log into in-memory widgets even when the signed-in user is a CASHIER who can never navigate to Admin. The role gating (isMgr/isAdmin, lines 96-97) only governs which nav actions/toolbuttons are created, not which pages are built or queried. This loads privileged data (user accounts, the HMAC-chained audit trail) into a cashier's process/session and incurs the query cost on every login. The PHP app never renders admin content for non-admins.
findings.recommendation: Construct manager/admin pages lazily and only for eligible roles: build cashier-reachable pages eagerly, and create Medicines/Inventory/Purchasing/Reports/Admin pages only inside the isMgr/isAdmin branches (or lazily on first navigation). Do not call reload()/reloadAudit()/reloadUsers() for a page the current role cannot open.

findings.title: Dashboard shows tiles for sections the cashier cannot reach; they silently no-op
findings.detail: DashboardPage is constructed with only the DB handle and no user/role (MainWindow.cpp:39), so it cannot gate its quick-action tiles. It renders tiles for Medicines, Inventory, Purchasing, Reports, and 'Admin and settings' to every user (DashboardPage.cpp:70-77). For a cashier, actionByTitle has no entry for those titles, so openSection() maps to no action and the click is a deliberate silent no-op (MainWindow.cpp:172-178). The PHP dashboard (pos/frontend/pages/home.php) wraps its action-cards and KPIs in `if ($isMgr)` / `if ($isAdmin)` so cashiers never see Inventory/Reports/Users cards. The Qt port presents dead buttons — a confusing UX regression and a parity deviation.
findings.recommendation: Pass the UserRecord (or role) into DashboardPage and gate the tile list the same way the PHP home.php gates action-cards (isMgr/isAdmin), so cashiers do not see Medicines/Inventory/Purchasing/Reports/Admin tiles. Alternatively, disable/hide tiles whose title is absent from the reachable action set.

findings.title: PHP primary nav 'History' and 'Day Close' have no clear equivalent in the Qt top nav
findings.detail: The PHP layout's $primary set (always visible to cashier+) is Dashboard, POS, History (/pos/history), Returns, Day Close (/pos/session). The Qt primary nav is Dashboard, POS, Returns, Sessions (MainWindow.cpp:134-139). 'Day Close'/shift maps plausibly to 'Sessions', but per-transaction sale History (/pos/history) — which the PHP dashboard KPIs also deep-link to ('Click for per-transaction sales history') — has no primary nav entry here. If sale history is only reachable via Reports (manager+), cashiers lose the ability to view transaction history they have in the PHP app.
findings.recommendation: Confirm where /pos/history is ported. If it is manager-gated under Reports, that is a downgrade from the PHP cashier-visible History; add a cashier-reachable History entry or fold it into the POS/Sessions page to preserve parity.

findings.title: No tests cover role-based nav gating or the sign-out session loop
findings.detail: The only place MainWindow is instantiated in tests is screenshots.cpp, and only with an ADMIN user (role = 'ADMIN', lines 197/205/306). There is no test that constructs MainWindow as CASHIER vs MANAGER vs ADMIN and asserts which nav actions exist (the Inventory dropdown, Reports, Admin), nor any test that the signedOut() signal fires and the main() forever-loop returns to login rather than quitting. Role gating is exactly the kind of access-control logic that should be regression-tested, especially given the eager-page-construction issue above.
findings.recommendation: Add a headless functional test that builds MainWindow for each role and asserts the set of present/absent QActions (by the actionByTitle keys), and asserts AdminPage is not reachable for non-admins. Add a test that emitting signedOut() triggers w.close() and the loop continues.

findings.title: installNotice (AppImage install/upgrade banner) is shown even if the operator cancels the first-run wizard
findings.detail: installIfAppImage() runs at line 88 and records first-install/upgrade. If db.isFirstRun() and the wizard is cancelled, main() returns 0 at line 94 — that path correctly skips the notice. But the notice is computed before the wizard; on the normal first-run path the desktop entry is installed and the notice queued before the user has committed to setting up the app. Minor: a user who completes desktop integration but abandons setup still has the .desktop/icon installed (harmless but slightly surprising). Lower priority, noting for completeness.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as-is for single-PC use; if tightening, defer installIfAppImage() until after the first-run wizard is accepted so desktop integration only happens for a configured app.

findings.title: Auto-backup runs inside MainWindow construction on every login, blocking the first paint
findings.detail: MainWindow's constructor synchronously runs BackupService::autoBackupIfDue() (lines 208-212), which copies the SQLite DB file off-machine when due. Because this is in the constructor (before showMaximized()/exec()), a due backup of a large DB stalls the window from appearing, on every login that crosses the due threshold. It also runs once per MainWindow instance, so each sign-in/sign-out cycle re-evaluates it.
findings.recommendation: Move the due-backup check to fire shortly after the window is shown (e.g. QTimer::singleShot(0,...) or on first idle) so the UI paints first; or run the file copy on a worker thread. Confirm 'due' is time-gated so repeated logins in one day don't re-trigger.

findings.title: Manager-only Inventory dropdown and Reports/Admin actions are not keyboard-discoverable consistently; grouped items lack shortcuts
findings.detail: Flat nav buttons get Ctrl+1..Ctrl+6 shortcuts, but the Inventory dropdown's grouped items (Medicines/Inventory/Purchasing via addGrouped, lines 150-159) get no shortcuts, and the Inventory QToolButton itself has none. This is a minor accelerator-parity inconsistency (the PHP app uses links, no shortcuts, so this is additive Qt behavior that's applied unevenly). Not a correctness issue.
findings.recommendation: Either give the grouped Inventory items their own accelerators or document that only top-level sections are keyboard-addressable; ensure the chosen scheme is consistent.

findings.title: Manager-override PIN verification has no brute-force throttle (regression vs PHP)
findings.detail: UserRepository::verifyManagerOverride (src/data/UserRepository.cpp:443-492) bcrypt-scans every active manager/admin against the entered PIN with NO rate limiting, lockout, or delay. The PHP source-of-truth (pos/backend/services/ManagerOverride.php:25-58) explicitly rate-limits this path: 'Rate-limited per PIN-attempt to defeat brute force' via RateLimit::check(...) returning 'Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.' before any verify, and RateLimit::reset on success. This override path authorizes discounts, voids, and return witnessing (PosTerminalPage.cpp:466-498, ReturnsPage.cpp:555). A cashier with terminal access can repeatedly submit guesses against a 6-8 digit PIN with no penalty — the only side effect is an OVERRIDE_DENIED audit row per attempt. This is a direct port-parity security regression on a privilege-escalation control.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the PHP RateLimit on the override path: throttle/lock by a per-terminal or global override key (e.g. reuse the failed_attempts/locked_until backoff, or a dedicated counter), reject with a wait message past a threshold, and reset on success. Add a test asserting repeated wrong override PINs eventually get throttled.

findings.title: Single-instance lock never reclaims a stale lock after a crash (setStaleLockTime(0))
findings.detail: main.cpp:53-59 creates QLockFile(dbPath + '.lock'), calls lock.setStaleLockTime(0) which DISABLES stale-lock detection, then tryLock(200). If the process dies hard (SIGKILL, OOM, power loss) the lock file is left on disk and is never considered stale, so every subsequent launch hits tryLock failure and shows '%1 is already running' and exits — the app becomes permanently unlaunchable until the user manually deletes the .lock file, which a pharmacy operator won't know to do. QLockFile records the owning PID/hostname and offers getLockInfo()/removeStaleLockFile() precisely for this, none of which are used.
findings.recommendation: Set a finite stale time (e.g. 30s) so QLockFile auto-reclaims, or on tryLock failure call getLockInfo() and verify the recorded PID is actually alive; if dead, removeStaleLockFile() and retry. Otherwise a single crash bricks the install for a non-technical user.

findings.title: Role enforcement is UI-only; backend repositories/pages perform no role check
findings.detail: Role gating is done purely by not creating nav buttons in MainWindow.cpp:96-170 (cashiers don't get Inventory/Reports/Admin actions). But every page object (AdminPage, InventoryPage, ReportsPage, etc.) is still constructed and added to the QStackedWidget for ALL users (MainWindow.cpp:39-57), and the data-access methods (UserRepository::createUser/updateUser/setPin, StockAdjuster, etc.) do not verify the acting user's role — they accept an actingUserId purely for the audit row. The PHP source-of-truth enforces authorization server-side per route via Auth::requireRole(...) → 403 (pos/backend/Auth.php:100-107). On a single-PC kiosk the practical exposure is lower, but any future entry point (dashboard tile, keyboard shortcut, programmatic showPage, or a code change that surfaces a page) would grant a cashier full admin/manager actions because the security boundary lives only in which buttons were drawn. SessionsPage/ReturnsPage do re-query role for sub-tabs, but Admin/user-management does not gate at the operation level.
findings.recommendation: Enforce role in the domain/data layer (e.g. UserRepository write methods assert the actingUser is ADMIN; adjustment/override services assert MANAGER/ADMIN) so authorization doesn't depend on UI construction, matching PHP's requireRole semantics. At minimum, don't instantiate admin-only pages for non-admins.

findings.title: zreport.key is silently regenerated on read failure, invalidating all prior Z-report signatures
findings.detail: ZReportArchive::secret() (src/service/ZReportArchive.cpp:17-40) reads the HMAC key from zreport.key; if the file is missing, unreadable, or empty (trimmed hex empty), it silently generates a fresh random 32-byte key and overwrites the file. Because Z-report integrity verification recomputes HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical payload with this key, a regenerated key makes EVERY previously archived signature fail verification with no warning — the exact opposite of the tamper-evidence the signed Z-report is meant to provide. A transient read error (permissions hiccup, partial write) thus destroys forensic continuity. There is also a TOCTOU: the same QFile handle is reused for the read-open and the write-open without re-checking existence under a lock, so two processes could both generate and one clobbers the other's key.
findings.recommendation: Treat a present-but-unreadable/empty key as a hard error (refuse to sign/verify, surface it) rather than silently minting a new one. Generate the key once at first-run/bootstrap, never lazily inside secret(). Open with exclusive create (O_EXCL semantics) to avoid the clobber race.

findings.title: hardenPermissions() omits the HMAC key file and logs directory
findings.detail: AppPaths::hardenPermissions() (src/domain/AppPaths.cpp:41-54) chmod 0700 the base dir and 0600 the db / -wal / -shm files only. It does NOT harden zreport.key (the HMAC secret) or the logs/ directory and its files. The key currently relies on being created with 0600 lazily inside ZReportArchive (ZReportArchive.cpp:37) and on the 0700 parent dir for containment, but if a legacy migration (migrateFrom, AppPaths.cpp:58-79) or external copy ever places these with looser modes they're never re-tightened, and logs (which can contain operational/error detail) inherit umask. Defense-in-depth: the hardening pass should explicitly cover every sensitive artifact, not just the DB.
findings.recommendation: Extend hardenPermissions() to also setPermissions(0600) on zreport.key and on logs/*.log, and 0700 on logs/. Run it (or re-run) after legacy migration copies files in.

findings.title: Login timing/lockout side-channel enables username enumeration
findings.detail: The UI message on login failure is correctly generic ('Invalid username or PIN.', LoginDialog.cpp:127), but two observable behaviors differ between existing and non-existing accounts: (1) LoginDialog::attempt (LoginDialog.cpp:120-132) only runs Bcrypt::verify when rec.valid is true — for an unknown username it returns immediately, so an attacker can distinguish real vs fake usernames by response latency (bcrypt cost-12 verify vs none). (2) registerFailedLogin (UserRepository.cpp:347-396) and secondsLockedOut (UserRepository.cpp:329-345) are no-ops for unknown/inactive users, so a valid username eventually shows 'Too many attempts. Try again in Ns.' while a bogus one never locks — a second enumeration oracle. The PHP app mitigates this by rate-limiting on BOTH a per-username and a per-IP key with a deliberate sleep (pos/backend/Auth.php:31-39, RateLimit.php).
findings.recommendation: Always perform a bcrypt verify against a fixed dummy hash when the user is not found (constant-time-ish path), and apply throttling on a generic key so locked/throttled feedback doesn't depend on whether the username exists.

findings.title: Audit JSON payloads built via string interpolation (audit-record integrity / injection into logs)
findings.detail: Audit detail JSON is assembled with QString::arg rather than a JSON serializer in several places: recordLogin (UserRepository.cpp:326 — {"username":"%1"}), createUser (UserRepository.cpp:180-181), and verifyManagerOverride (UserRepository.cpp:483,489). A username/action containing a double-quote, backslash, or control char produces malformed/forgeable JSON in the append-only audit_log. The username validator in LoginDialog restricts the live login field to [A-Za-z0-9._-], but recordLogin is fed the raw submitted string and other call sites (createUser via UserDialog, override action labels) are not guaranteed to be so constrained. Since audit_log is the tamper-evidence trail for a medical-retail system, malformed/injectable entries weaken its evidentiary value.
findings.recommendation: Build these payloads with QJsonObject/QJsonDocument (or at least escape the values) so the stored audit JSON is always well-formed and not attacker-shapeable.

findings.title: No security regression tests for override throttle, role enforcement, or login timing
findings.detail: tests/cases/auth_tests.cpp covers the login lockout (registerFailedLogin/secondsLockedOut/clearFailedLogins) and pinpolicy_tests covers PIN strength, which is good. But there is no test asserting that verifyManagerOverride is throttled (it currently isn't — see the high finding), no test that a CASHIER cannot perform admin/manager data operations (role boundary), and no test that login response/lockout behavior is identical for known vs unknown usernames (enumeration). Given CLAUDE.md mandates tests on security-sensitive paths and bit-for-bit PHP parity, these are the gaps most likely to let a regression slip through.
findings.recommendation: Add cases: (a) repeated wrong manager-override PINs get rejected/throttled and a correct PIN still works after reset; (b) UserRepository write methods reject a non-admin actingUserId once role checks are added; (c) lockout/timing parity between existing and non-existing usernames.

findings.title: Test suite is not wired into CTest and there is no CI — green tests are unenforced
findings.detail: CMakeLists.txt builds pharmadesk_tests, pharmadesk_smoke, pharmadesk_shots, and pharmadesk_barcode_test, but contains no enable_testing()/add_test() (grep for ctest/add_test/enable_testing returns nothing), so `ctest` runs zero tests. There is no .github/workflows, no .gitlab-ci, and no shell runner script anywhere in the repo (find for *.sh / CI yml is empty). The full suite's pass/fail is only visible if a human manually runs ./pharmadesk_tests and reads stdout. For a medical-retail money/stock system this means a regression in the FEFO or Money path can be committed and packaged into the AlmaLinux AppImage with nothing gating it.
findings.recommendation: Add enable_testing() and add_test(NAME suite COMMAND pharmadesk_tests) (plus pharmadesk_barcode_test) so `ctest` fails the build on a red suite. Add a minimal CI job (or at least a tests/run.sh) that builds with -DBUILD_TESTING=ON and runs ctest --output-on-failure, mirroring the PHP tests/run.php convention.

findings.title: Money invariant validated with floating-point (CAST AS REAL + toDouble + 0.005 epsilon)
findings.detail: returns_tests.cpp computes COMPLETED-sales totals with `SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CAST(grand_total AS REAL)),0)`, converts with `.toDouble()`, and asserts `qAbs((totalBefore - totalAfter) - 38.0) < 0.005`. This directly contradicts CLAUDE.md's 'never floating point for stored monetary values' rule. A 0.004 rounding divergence from PHP would silently pass, and CAST-to-REAL of a TEXT decimal column can lose precision — exactly the class of bug the fixed-point Money type exists to prevent. The rest of the money tests correctly use Money/string comparisons, so this is an isolated but load-bearing lapse on the void/totals path.
findings.recommendation: Compare the void delta using Money string arithmetic (SUM the grand_total TEXT values via the repository/Money, assert exact '38.00'), not REAL/double with an epsilon.

findings.title: HMAC-signed Z-report has no tamper/verify test (and no verify API)
findings.detail: printing_tests.cpp tests ZReportArchive::signAndStore for signature length (64 hex), idempotency, and single-row storage, but never verifies that the signature actually detects tampering — there is no test that mutates a stored Z-report (or session totals) and confirms verification fails. ZReportArchive.h exposes only signAndStore() and no verify()/recompute() method, so the PHP /zreport/verify/{id} integrity guarantee is neither implemented as a checkable API nor covered by a negative test. A signed-but-unverifiable report provides false assurance for an end-of-shift financial control.
findings.recommendation: Add a verify(sessionId, signatureHex) path to ZReportArchive and a test that (a) accepts the freshly-signed value and (b) rejects after the underlying session figures are altered, matching the PHP verify route.

findings.title: Printing/ops services untested: CupsStatus, CupsRawPrinter, DesktopIntegration
findings.detail: src/service/CupsStatus.cpp, CupsRawPrinter.cpp, and src/domain/DesktopIntegration.cpp have zero references in tests/ (grep across tests returns nothing for Cups/DesktopIntegration). printing_tests.cpp covers EscPosRenderer, ZReportArchive, and AlternativesFinder only. These are the AlmaLinux-target integration surfaces (raw CUPS printing, printer status polling shown in AdminPage, .desktop/icon install) where a single-PC deployment is most likely to break, and they ship untested. At minimum the pure/parse-able parts (CUPS status string parsing, desktop-file content generation) are unit-testable without hardware.
findings.recommendation: Extract and test the parseable logic (CUPS lpstat/status parsing, .desktop file generation, printer-name resolution) with fixture inputs; gate the hardware-dependent send behind an interface so the renderer-to-bytes path is asserted even without a printer.

findings.title: No test for transaction rollback when a sale fails mid-commit (atomicity)
findings.detail: sale_tests.cpp verifies that an UP-FRONT insufficient-stock rejection leaves stock unchanged (the validation-fails-before-writes case). It does not exercise a failure that occurs AFTER partial writes (e.g. a constraint/trigger failure on the second of multiple FEFO batch decrements, or an inventory_movements insert failing) to prove the whole transaction rolls back with no partial stock decrement, no orphan sale_items, and no half-written ledger. Given CLAUDE.md's hard requirement that 'never leave stock in an inconsistent state on error,' the all-or-nothing guarantee is the single most important reliability property and is currently only inferred, not tested.
findings.recommendation: Add a fault-injection test: force a failure partway through a multi-batch sale commit (e.g. via a trigger or a deliberately violated CHECK) and assert sales/sale_items/inventory_movements/batches are all unchanged from the pre-sale snapshot.

findings.title: Audit chain integrity untested; HMAC chain explicitly deferred (parity gap vs PHP append-only chain)
findings.detail: Audit.h states 'HMAC chain (prev_hmac/row_hmac) is deferred to the Phase-6 Audit port.' Tests cover only that the audit_log table rejects UPDATE/DELETE via trigger (schema_tests.cpp) and that some actions write rows (smoke.cpp). There is no test that audit rows are written for the security-critical events the PHP app chains (sale commit, stock adjustment, void/return, PIN change, login lockout) with the expected actor/action/entity, and no chain-continuity test. CLAUDE.md says the HMAC chain may be simplified for single-PC SQLite but the audit records must be kept — that 'records exist for who-did-what-when on sales and stock adjustments' assertion is not verified.
findings.recommendation: Add audit assertions to the sale, adjustment, and returns integration tests confirming an audit_log row with the correct action_type/entity/actor is written per operation; if the simplified chain is intended to ship, add at least one continuity/ordering test so the immutability trigger isn't the only coverage.

findings.title: Screenshots harness has no assertions or baseline — it is manual review, not a test
findings.detail: tests/screenshots.cpp (built as pharmadesk_shots) grabs each screen under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen and saves PNGs, but performs no assertions, has no golden-image baseline, and always returns 0 (line 315). It will pass even if a screen renders blank or throws after construction. It is useful for human visual review but is misleading as part of a 'test' target and provides no regression protection for the 'match the existing UI' fidelity goal.
findings.recommendation: Either keep it explicitly as a non-test tool (rename target/doc as a screenshot generator), or add lightweight assertions (each grabbed QImage is non-null and non-uniform/non-blank) and a return code so a crash-on-open is caught in automation.

findings.title: Money::div-by-zero parity: PHP throws DivisionByZeroError, C++ divByInt returns 0 and the test bakes in the divergence
findings.detail: PHP Money::div() throws \DivisionByZeroError (Money.php:55) and the PHP suite asserts the throw. The C++ port has no Money::div; CostBlender uses Money::divByInt(0) which returns zero, and money_tests.cpp:565 asserts `divByInt(0).isZero()`. The test therefore documents/locks-in a deliberate behavioral divergence from the source-of-truth spec rather than flagging it. CostBlender guards the divisor upstream so the end-to-end result still matches PHP's zero-base-units case, so this is low severity — but the test gives false confidence of parity where the primitive semantics actually differ.
findings.recommendation: Add a comment in money_tests.cpp documenting the intentional divergence and the upstream guard, or (cleaner) make the divisor-zero policy explicit and assert the CostBlender end-to-end golden values directly so the parity claim rests on the blended result, not on the silently-different primitive.

findings.title: All build/packaging tools fetched from unpinned ":continuous" tags with no checksum verification (supply-chain + reproducibility)
findings.detail: packaging/build-appimage.sh:30-35,180-181 downloads linuxdeploy-x86_64.AppImage, linuxdeploy-plugin-qt, appimagetool, and runtime-x86_64 all from GitHub "…/releases/download/continuous/…" URLs. The fetch() helper (lines 24-29) does `curl -fSL` then `chmod +x` with NO SHA256 verification, and skips re-download if the file already exists (`[ -x "$2" ] && return 0`). 'continuous' is a moving target rebuilt on every upstream commit, so two builds days apart silently use different tooling — the output AppImage is not reproducible, and a compromised/regressed upstream binary is executed against your AppDir with zero integrity check. For a medical-retail product this is the weakest link in the release chain.
findings.recommendation: Pin each tool to a specific tagged release (not 'continuous') and verify a known SHA256 in fetch() before chmod +x (curl the .sha256 or hardcode the digest; fail the build on mismatch). Document the pinned versions in the script header. Re-pin deliberately, not implicitly.

findings.title: Product version is hardcoded (0.1.0) with no git/tag linkage — easy to ship a build mislabeled as the wrong version
findings.detail: CMakeLists.txt:2 sets `project(pharmadesk VERSION 0.1.0)` and passes it through PHARMADESK_VERSION (line 122). DesktopIntegration.cpp:201-214 uses Branding::appVersion() as the source of truth for the first-install-vs-upgrade decision (settings InstalledVersion) and the user-facing "Updated to vX" notice. Nothing ties the version to a VCS tag or build metadata (and the project isn't even a git repo per `ls .git`). It is trivial to cut an AppImage from uncommitted/edited source that still reports 0.1.0, so the upgrade-detection logic and the About box can lie about what code is actually running — a real problem when supporting a deployed pharmacy PC remotely.
findings.recommendation: Derive the version from `git describe --tags --dirty` (or an injected CI variable) at configure time and fall back to project() VERSION only when VCS info is unavailable; append a short commit hash to the displayed build string. Initialize a git repo / tag releases so versions are traceable.

findings.title: Only the X11 (xcb) Qt platform plugin is bundled — no Wayland plugin; risky on AlmaLinux 10's Wayland-default GNOME
findings.detail: The build sets EXTRA_PLATFORM_PLUGINS=libqoffscreen.so (build-appimage.sh:49) and linuxdeploy-plugin-qt bundles xcb by default. Verified in AppDir/usr/plugins/platforms: only libqxcb.so and libqoffscreen.so are present — no libqwayland*.so, and no wayland platforminputcontext. AlmaLinux 10 ships GNOME on Wayland by default. The app will run via XWayland (xcb under a Wayland compositor), which usually works, but you lose native Wayland behavior (HiDPI scaling, fractional scaling, proper window/dock association) and depend on XWayland being installed/enabled. Since the target box is fixed and known, this is a deliberate-decision-worth-documenting rather than a guaranteed bug.
findings.recommendation: Either explicitly bundle the Qt Wayland platform plugin (add to EXTRA_PLATFORM_PLUGINS and ensure its deps come along) so the app runs natively under Wayland, OR document that the AppImage targets XWayland and confirm XWayland is present on the AlmaLinux 10 image. At minimum verify the dock-icon/StartupWMClass mapping (DesktopIntegration sets StartupWMClass) actually works under the deployed session type.

findings.title: No post-build self-test of the produced AppImage — a broken bundle can ship undetected
findings.detail: build-appimage.sh configures with -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF (line 38) so the test/smoke executables are not even built in the release path, and the script ends at `ls -lh …AppImage` (line 190) with no verification that the packaged binary launches. The whole ICU-minimization step rewrites libicudata.so by carving an ELF blob and rebuilding it (lines 112-159); it self-checks only `nm -D | grep icudt_dat` (line 157) inside the subshell, not that Qt/SQLite actually initialize against the trimmed data. Given the offscreen platform plugin is bundled specifically for headless runs (comment, line 48), nothing exercises it. A regression in bundling (missing lib, bad ICU repack, dropped sqldriver) would only be caught when the pharmacy PC fails to start.
findings.recommendation: After packaging, run a smoke launch of the final AppImage headless, e.g. `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./PharmaDesk-x86_64.AppImage --self-test` (add a tiny flag that opens the DB, runs a trivial Qt SQL query, and exits non-zero on failure) and fail the build if it doesn't pass. Also build+run pharmadesk_tests in a separate configure step before producing the release image.

findings.title: No static-analysis or sanitizer build path, and warnings are non-fatal — defects in the money/stock/FEFO core can slip through
findings.detail: CMakeLists.txt enables -Wall -Wextra (lines 9-11) but deliberately not -Werror (comment lines 7-8), and there is no clang-tidy hook (CMAKE_CXX_CLANG_TIDY), no cppcheck integration, and no ASan/UBSan build option anywhere in the tree (grep for sanitize/tidy/cppcheck/IPO/LTO returns nothing). For a fixed-point Money type doing manual decimal/string math, FEFO batch selection, and stock-ledger arithmetic, an ASan/UBSan run over the 1000+ assertion suite (pharmadesk_tests) would catch integer overflow, signed-overflow UB, and use-after-free that -Wextra cannot. The 'don't -Werror so a stray MOC warning never blocks the deployment box' rationale conflates the dev/test build with the release build — there's no separate strict mode for the code you own.
findings.recommendation: Add an option(ENABLE_SANITIZERS) that compiles pharmadesk_core + pharmadesk_tests with -fsanitize=address,undefined for the test run, and an option(ENABLE_TIDY) wiring CMAKE_CXX_CLANG_TIDY on the core library (excluding MOC/generated). Keep release builds as-is. Treat warnings in your own translation units as errors via a per-target property if you don't want it global.

findings.title: AppImage is not reproducible (timestamps/parallelism/build-host paths embedded), undermining provenance
findings.detail: Beyond the unpinned tools (separate finding): the script never sets SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, mksquashfs is invoked without -mkfs-time/-all-time normalization (line 184), genccode+gcc rebuild libicudata fresh each run, and the qmake-wrap and qtplugins symlink farm embed the absolute build-host plugin path ($pluginsrc) into generated artifacts. CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release with default flags can also embed __FILE__ build paths. Two builds of the identical source therefore won't be bit-identical, so you can't independently re-derive and verify a shipped AppImage's hash — a meaningful integrity property for a system handling controlled-substance records.
findings.recommendation: Export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (e.g. from git commit date), pass mksquashfs `-all-time $SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH -mkfs-time $SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, add -ffile-prefix-map to strip build paths, and publish the resulting SHA256 alongside each release so the deployment can be verified.

findings.title: .desktop entry omits the freedesktop Version key (and Keywords); not validated against desktop-file-validate
findings.detail: packaging/pharmadesk.desktop (and the identical AppDir copy) has no `Version=` key — desktop-file-validate emits a warning for this and some stricter menu tools reject entries lacking it. There are also no Keywords (discoverability in the apps menu) and no StartupWMClass in the bundled file itself (DesktopIntegration.cpp:123-124 adds it at install time, but the in-AppImage entry used by some integrators lacks it). The build never runs desktop-file-validate, so spec drift goes unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Add `Version=1.5` (the desktop-entry spec version, not the app version), `Keywords=pharmacy;pos;inventory;`, and a StartupWMClass to packaging/pharmadesk.desktop, and run `desktop-file-validate` on it as a build step (fail on error). Keep the runtime rewrite of Exec/StartupWMClass as-is.

findings.title: Default (non-AppImage) builds get no optimization and no defined build type; dev/test results may not match the shipped Release binary
findings.detail: CMakeLists.txt never sets a default CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE, so a plain `cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build` (the obvious dev/test invocation) produces an unoptimized, no-NDEBUG build. Only build-appimage.sh forces -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release. This means the money/FEFO test suite developers run locally compiles with different optimization (and different floating/integer codegen edge cases, ordering, and UB exposure) than the binary that actually ships. It also means no LTO/IPO is ever applied to the release binary, leaving size/perf on the table for an app whose size was specifically optimized (memory note: 36MB→26MB effort).
findings.recommendation: Add the standard guard to set CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE to RelWithDebInfo when unset, so dev/test and release share representative codegen; optionally enable CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION (LTO) for the Release config after confirming it links cleanly with the Qt5/Qt6 fallback.

findings.title: Audit-log write failures are silently swallowed — breaks append-only audit guarantee and PHP parity
findings.detail: Audit::write (src/data/Audit.cpp:9) returns bool, but all 27 call sites ignore it (e.g. SaleService.cpp:347, ReturnService.cpp:280/435/505/682/810, StockAdjuster.cpp:165, Reconciler.cpp:93). If the audit INSERT fails (CHECK violation, disk-full, future immutability trigger), the surrounding transaction still proceeds to commit() and succeeds, so the sale/return/adjustment persists with NO audit record. The PHP source treats this as fatal: Audit::write -> Db::execute runs under PDO ERRMODE_EXCEPTION, so a failed audit INSERT throws and aborts the whole transaction (../pos/backend/Audit.php). This is a who-did-what-when guarantee for a controlled-substance/medical retail system; the port weakens it from 'sale and audit are atomic' to 'sale commits, audit is best-effort'.
findings.recommendation: Make callers check the return: wrap Audit::write in the same 'if (!...) throw XError{...}' pattern used for every other query in these services, so a failed audit write rolls back the enclosing transaction exactly as PHP does. Add a test that forces an audit failure and asserts the sale did not commit.

findings.title: Single-instance lock disables stale detection — a hard crash locks the user out permanently
findings.detail: main.cpp:54 calls lock.setStaleLockTime(0). Per Qt docs, a stale time of 0 means QLockFile NEVER considers a lock stale. If the process dies without releasing the lock (SIGKILL, OOM killer, power loss, AppImage crash) the <db>.lock file and its embedded PID survive, and every subsequent launch hits tryLock()==false -> 'PharmaDesk is already running' (main.cpp:55-58) and exits. On a single-PC pharmacy till this is a hard outage with no in-app recovery; the operator must know to delete a hidden lock file. Qt's default (30s) plus QLockFile::getLockInfo()/removeStaleLockFile() detects a dead PID and recovers automatically.
findings.recommendation: Drop setStaleLockTime(0) (use the default) or set a modest window, and on tryLock failure call getLockInfo() to check whether the recorded PID is alive; if dead, removeStaleLockFile() and retry. Surface a clear message only when a live instance is genuinely detected.

findings.title: PRAGMA synchronous left at WAL default (NORMAL) — last committed sale can be lost on power loss
findings.detail: Database::open (src/data/Database.cpp:26-27) sets foreign_keys=ON and journal_mode=WAL but never sets PRAGMA synchronous. In WAL mode SQLite's default is NORMAL, which does NOT fsync the WAL on every commit — a power loss or hard reset can lose the most recently committed transaction(s) (the data is durable only across application crashes, not OS/power crashes). For a cash-handling pharmacy till (a committed sale that decremented stock and took cash can vanish), and given AlmaLinux 10 PCs without guaranteed UPS, FULL is the safer choice and the performance cost on a single-PC workload is negligible.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly set PRAGMA synchronous = FULL (or at minimum keep NORMAL but document the durability trade-off and ensure a UPS). Set it right after journal_mode in Database::open and assert it succeeded.

findings.title: No tests exercise transaction rollback / partial-failure recovery despite CLAUDE.md mandate
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md requires: 'All sales and stock changes go through DB transactions; never leave stock in an inconsistent state on error' and 'Don't skip tests on the money/stock/expiry paths.' The test suite (tests/cases/*) covers business-rule rejections (e.g. adjustment_tests.cpp:188 quarantine refusal, returns_tests.cpp:283 over-return blocked) — all of which fail BEFORE or via clean validation. None inject a failure partway through a committed transaction (e.g. a forced UPDATE/INSERT error after the batch decrement but before commit) to prove the rollback actually restores batches.current_qty and leaves no orphan inventory_movements/sale_items row. The rollback code is correct on inspection, but the most safety-critical reliability property of the app is entirely unverified.
findings.recommendation: Add tests that force a mid-transaction SQL failure (e.g. point an insert at a temporarily-dropped column, or use a CHECK that trips on the second line) in SaleService::commit and ReturnService::voidSale, then assert: batch current_qty unchanged, no sale_items/inventory_movements rows written, sale row absent, and res.ok==false with the right message.

findings.title: Raw SQLite error strings are surfaced to cashiers as user-facing messages
findings.detail: On any infrastructure failure the services set res.error to the raw driver text, e.g. SaleService.cpp:236 'throw SaleError{q.lastError().text()}' (also lines 203,257,287,313,330,373 and the analogous lines in ReturnService/GrnService/StockAdjuster/Reconciler). The UI then shows that verbatim: PosTerminalPage.cpp:514 QMessageBox::warning(..., r.error), ReturnsPage.cpp:567/597/687/770, GrnDialog.cpp:177, etc. A cashier mid-sale can see 'UNIQUE constraint failed: sales.receipt_number' or 'database is locked' with no actionable guidance, while the genuinely useful detail (which is what should hit the log) is not logged at all. This is both a UX/professionalism gap and a minor information-leak.
findings.recommendation: Split the two audiences: log the raw lastError().text() (via the Log handler) and present a fixed, friendly message to the user ('Could not save the sale — please retry; details were recorded in the log.'). Keep the specific validation messages (qty, discount, stock) user-facing since those are intentional and actionable.

findings.title: try/catch around app.exec() cannot catch exceptions thrown in Qt event handlers
findings.detail: main.cpp:106-151 wraps the session loop (including app.exec()) in try/catch(std::exception) that logs and shows a dialog. Qt6 does not propagate C++ exceptions through the event loop: an exception thrown inside a slot/event handler during app.exec() is undefined behaviour and goes straight to std::terminate, NOT to this catch. So the handler only catches exceptions thrown in the thin login/PIN/MainWindow-construction code between event loops. In practice the services swallow their own throws (InsufficientStockException, std::runtime_error from Fefo::assertSortedByExpiry, SaleError) inside their try/catch, so reachable throws are contained — but any future unguarded throw in a UI slot dies via std::set_terminate (main.cpp:41) with an abort and no DB rollback. The set_terminate logger is the right mitigation; the misleading impression that app.exec() is exception-protected is the risk.
findings.recommendation: Either subclass QApplication and override notify() to wrap event dispatch in try/catch (the supported Qt pattern for catching slot exceptions and rolling back/logging), or document that the main.cpp try/catch only guards the between-loops code and rely on per-service guards + set_terminate. Add a regression note so no one assumes slot throws are caught here.

findings.title: Backup copies the main DB file only after a checkpoint that is not verified — risk of an inconsistent/partial backup
findings.detail: BackupService::backupNow (src/service/BackupService.cpp:27) runs 'PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)' then QFile::copy of the main .sqlite (lines 29-34), and does NOT copy the -wal/-shm sidecars. The checkpoint result is ignored: if a checkpoint is blocked (e.g. an open read transaction from a list view still holding the connection, or a busy return) TRUNCATE can fail or be partial, leaving committed data still in the WAL that the file-copy will miss — producing a backup that silently lacks the most recent transactions. Single-instance reduces but does not eliminate this (the same process can hold an open SELECT cursor).
findings.recommendation: Use SQLite's online backup API (QSqlDatabase doesn't expose it directly, so either use sqlite3_backup via the native handle, or VACUUM INTO 'backup.sqlite' which produces a guaranteed-consistent single-file snapshot regardless of WAL state). At minimum, check the wal_checkpoint return (busy/log/checkpointed counts) and fail the backup loudly if it didn't fully checkpoint.

findings.title: Receipt/return/GRN/adjustment number generation falls back to a random suffix that breaks monotonic numbering on contention
findings.detail: nextReceiptNumber (SaleService.cpp:50-52) and the analogous nextReturnNumber/nextGrnNumber/nextAdjustmentNumber compute count(*)+1 outside any unique-claim, and on a collision fall back to a 6-digit RANDOM suffix ('INV-yyyymmdd-<rand%1000000>') rather than failing. The sequence is also generated INSIDE the transaction in SaleService (line 207, good) but the count() is a non-atomic read. The schema has a UNIQUE constraint, so duplicates won't persist, but the random-fallback produces non-sequential, non-auditable document numbers (a gap a regulator/accountant would flag) and masks the real problem instead of retrying the count. On a single-PC single-instance system collisions are unlikely, but a same-second double-submit (double-click on Complete Sale) can trigger it.
findings.recommendation: On a unique-constraint collision, retry the count-based sequence a few times (as nextReturnNumber already does with attempt+N) before any fallback, and prefer a clean failure ('Could not allocate a receipt number, please retry') over a random suffix so numbering stays sequential and auditable. Also debounce/disable the Complete button during commit to avoid same-second double submits.

findings.title: Qt barcode parser supports only 4 of the PHP parser's formats — HIBC, IFA PPN, China eCode, ISO 15434 envelope all dropped
findings.detail: PHP QrParser.php (721 lines) decodes GS1 AI strings (strict + heuristic), GS1 Digital Link, HIBC LIC (+secondary $$ date/lot), IFA PPN (9N), China NMPA eCode (20-digit), ISO 15434 envelope ([)>RS06...), free-text 'Batch No / Exp.Date' labels, plus NHRN, SSCC, production/best-before dates, GTIN check-digit validation, and symbology guessing. The Qt domain/BarcodeParser.cpp (336 lines, enum Type { PlainText, GTIN, GS1, GS1DigitalLink }) handles only Digital Link, GS1 AI strings, bare GTIN, and plain text. Scanning an HIBC/PPN/China-eCode/ISO-15434 pack yields no GTIN extraction, so MedicineRepository::searchForPos() cannot match primary_barcode and the scan falls through to a free-text LIKE on the whole code string (no match). For a pharmacy expected to scan imported/device packs, this silently breaks scanning of those packs.
findings.recommendation: Port the remaining QrParser branches (parseHibc, parsePpn, parseIso15434, China eCode, parseFreeText) and the auxiliary fields (lot/expiry/serial/NHRN/SSCC, check_digit_ok) into BarcodeParser, or explicitly document and scope-out the unsupported symbologies with the customer. At minimum extract the GTIN from HIBC/PPN/ISO-15434 so primary_barcode matching works.

findings.title: POS 'scan → auto-add → next scan' workflow and parsed-barcode chip/heuristic warning are missing
findings.detail: PHP pos/terminal.php (search action, lines 60-125) auto-adds to the cart when a structured barcode scan matches exactly one in-stock medicine, merging repeat scans of the same unit/price into a single qty-incremented line ('scan, scan, scan' = qty 3). It also renders a barcode chip showing the decoded GTIN/Lot/Exp/SN and a 'heuristic — verify lot/exp' warning badge when the scanner dropped the FNC1 separator (GS1_AI_HEURISTIC). Qt PosTerminalPage::runSearch() only populates a results table from the raw text; there is no auto-add on scan, no merge-on-rescan, and no chip/heuristic warning surfaced anywhere. The cashier must manually select + click 'Add unit' for every scan, and the safety prompt to double-check a heuristically-parsed lot/expiry is gone.
findings.recommendation: Detect a structured-barcode scan in runSearch (Barcode::parse(...).isBarcode), and when exactly one in-stock hit results, auto-add 1 base unit and merge into an existing matching line. Surface the parsed lot/expiry and the heuristic warning (e.g. an inline banner) so cashiers verify boundary-guessed fields before completing the sale.

findings.title: Audit-log viewer is much weaker than PHP /reports/audit — no filter, no pagination, no CSV export, no HMAC/tamper-evident column
findings.detail: PHP reports/audit.php offers a filterable (action_type ILIKE, entity_type), paginated, CSV-exportable audit viewer that surfaces actor, IP, before/after JSON, and an HMAC-ok column (badge ✓ OK / ⚠ FAIL via length(row_hmac)=64) — the tamper-evidence is the whole point of the append-only HMAC-chained log. The Qt equivalent (AdminPage Audit tab + AuditRepository::list) is a read-only last-500 dump of When/User/Action/Entity/ID only: no filter, no pagination beyond 500, no CSV export, and no HMAC/tamper indicator. For a medical-retail compliance audit this is a meaningful capability loss.
findings.recommendation: Add action/entity filters, paging (or a date-range), CSV export, and a per-row integrity indicator to the audit viewer. If the HMAC chain is simplified per CLAUDE.md, still show an integrity/'verified' column derived from whatever chain field exists, plus before/after detail on row open.

findings.title: Dedicated Expiry and Low-stock report screens are missing (downgraded to dashboard KPIs only)
findings.detail: PHP has standalone /reports/expiry and /reports/low-stock screens (in routes.php and reports/expiry.php, reports/low-stock.php) — filterable, sortable, exportable operational reports a pharmacist uses to drive write-offs and reorders. Qt's ReportsPage tabs are Sales, P&L, Top sellers, Tax, Refunds, Compliance, Velocity, Narcotic register — no Expiry or Low-stock tab. The only equivalent is a non-exportable top-8 shortlist + count KPI on DashboardPage (expiringSoon(60), lowStock(0)). A manager cannot pull a full, date/threshold-tunable, CSV-exportable expiry or low-stock list.
findings.recommendation: Add Expiry and Low-stock report tabs to ReportsPage backed by AnalyticsRepository/InventoryRepository, with configurable window/threshold, full listing, and CSV export to match the PHP reports.

findings.title: Missing free-text 'Batch No / Exp.Date' label parsing degrades hand-keyed batch entry
findings.detail: PHP QrParser::parseFreeText recognizes hand-typed or photographed package text like 'Batch No: X   Exp.Date: dd/mm/yyyy' and returns structured batch/expiry fields (type FREE_TEXT) used to pre-fill lot/expiry. The Qt parser has no FREE_TEXT branch — any such input falls straight through to PlainText with no batch/expiry extraction. Lower impact than the symbology gap but it is a real PHP capability with no Qt equivalent.
