findings.recommendation: Port parseFreeText (and its Julian/date helpers) so typed batch/expiry labels are recognized, or confirm with the customer that only scanner input is in scope.

findings.title: Sale-history 'Return from receipt' deep-link parity should be confirmed
findings.detail: PHP pos/history.php exposes a per-row 'Return' link to /pos/returns?receipt=<n> (hidden once REFUNDED_FULL/VOIDED) and a Reprint action; this is the primary path a cashier uses to start a refund against a specific historical sale. Qt's Sales report tab provides reprint (double-click) and a Refunds tab/ReturnsPage exists, but the direct 'start a return for this receipt' affordance from the sales list was not observed in ReportsPage. Verify the cashier can launch a return pre-scoped to a selected historical receipt without manually re-entering the receipt number.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Return…' row action on the Sales report (and/or a receipt-number prefill into ReturnsPage), gated the same way PHP gates it (hidden for REFUNDED_FULL/VOIDED), to match the history-screen workflow.

findings.title: README run/test commands reference non-existent binaries (cphc_smoke, cphc_shots)
findings.detail: The README's runnable snippets tell the reader to run `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./build/cphc_smoke` and `./build/cphc_shots screenshots`, and the status line says 'Headless smoke test (cphc_smoke, 90 checks)'. The actual built binaries are named `pharmadesk_smoke` and `pharmadesk_shots` (confirmed via `ls build/` and CMake targets). The `cphc_*` names do not exist anywhere, so every documented test/screenshot command fails out-of-the-box. This is the single most damaging doc bug because the snippets are presented as authoritative copy-paste blocks.
findings.recommendation: Update all four references to the real target names (pharmadesk_smoke, pharmadesk_shots). Better: rename binaries OR README consistently and add a one-line check in CI that the README's `./build/<name>` snippets resolve to real CMake targets so they cannot silently drift again.

findings.title: No documented backup RESTORE / disaster-recovery procedure despite shipped auto-backup
findings.detail: README advertises automated SQLite backup (WAL-checkpoint + copy off-machine, daily on startup + Backup-now), and src/service/BackupService.cpp implements the copy but contains no 'restore' code path (grep for 'restore' returns nothing). There is no runbook telling the pharmacy operator how to recover after a disk failure: where backups land, how to verify integrity, how to swap a backup back into ~/.local/share/PharmaDesk/.../pharmadesk.sqlite, or how to handle WAL/SHM sidecar files during restore. For a single-PC medical-retail system whose only data-loss mitigation is this backup, an untested/undocumented restore is the highest operational risk in this area.
findings.recommendation: Add a short OPS/RESTORE section (or docs/RUNBOOK.md): backup location, how to validate a backup (open read-only + integrity_check), exact stop-app / copy-file / restart steps including the -wal/-shm files, and a note that restore should be rehearsed once on the target machine before go-live.

findings.title: Status list marks built modules as deferred / not-done
findings.detail: README has an unchecked '[ ] Deferred triggers (DRAP narcotic gate, supplier-returns, parked bills, concurrency)' line and never mentions Returns, Cashier Sessions, Z-Report, Stock Adjustments, or Parked Bills as delivered. The source tree contradicts this: src/ui/ReturnsPage, SessionsPage, ZReportDialog, AdjustmentsPage, ParkedBillsDialog all exist, with matching services (ReturnService, Reconciler, StockAdjuster, ZReportArchive) and test cases (returns_tests.cpp, sessions_tests.cpp, parked_tests.cpp, adjustment_tests.cpp). The status section therefore badly understates completion and would mislead a reviewer/operator about what is usable.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the status checklist with the actual modules: add Returns / Sessions / Z-Report / Adjustments / Parked-bills phases and tick what is implemented; keep genuinely-deferred items (e.g. concurrency hardening, DRAP narcotic gate if still partial) as a clearly-scoped TODO.

findings.title: Primary unit-test suite (pharmadesk_tests, 19 case files) is undocumented
findings.detail: README documents only the smoke test. The real correctness coverage lives in pharmadesk_tests with 19 case files under tests/cases/ (money_tests, salecalc_tests, fefo_tests, sale_tests, returns_tests, costblender_tests, schema_tests, etc.) — exactly the money/stock/FEFO paths CLAUDE.md mandates be tested. A new engineer reading the README has no idea this suite exists or how to run it (./build/pharmadesk_tests), so the project's strongest quality asset is invisible and could rot unrun.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Run the test suite' subsection documenting `cmake --build build -j && ./build/pharmadesk_tests`, list the high-value areas it covers (money/FEFO/sale/returns), and note BUILD_TESTING is ON by default (and OFF for AppImage builds).

findings.title: Missing LICENSE and CHANGELOG files
findings.detail: Repo root has no LICENSE and no CHANGELOG. The bundled AppImage ships Qt6 (LGPL/GPL obligations), libxcrypt (bcrypt), ICU, and a rebuilt/minified libicudata — all of which carry attribution/relicensing terms — yet there is no license file for the app itself nor a third-party notices file documenting the bundled libraries' licenses. There is also no changelog to record what shipped in each phase, which the dense README status list is currently (and unreliably) doubling as.
findings.recommendation: Add a LICENSE for the project, plus a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES (or AppImage-bundled licenses dir) covering Qt6, libxcrypt, ICU, linuxdeploy/appimagetool runtime. Start a CHANGELOG.md (Keep-a-Changelog style) and move phase history out of the README status block.

findings.title: Inconsistent table counts across docs (17 vs 14 vs actual 18)
findings.detail: README claims 'schema port of all 17 tables', docs/PHP_APP_MAP.md:50 says the Postgres source has '14 tables' (while its own table list enumerates ~17), and sql/schema_sqlite.sql actually contains 18 CREATE TABLE statements. The numbers disagree three ways, which undermines confidence that the schema port is complete/tracked. (Worth a quick reconcile against ../db/schema/init.sql to confirm nothing was dropped or silently added during the port.)
findings.recommendation: Pick the authoritative count from the SQLite schema, fix both docs to match, and ideally enumerate the table list once (in PHP_APP_MAP) and reference it rather than repeating a bare number.

findings.title: AppImage size and README Layout tree are stale
findings.detail: README states the AppImage is '~35 MB'; the actual artifact is 26 MB (the size-optimization work in user memory landed but the doc wasn't updated). Separately, the 'Layout' tree only shows main.cpp/MainWindow plus a parenthetical '(data/ domain/ ui/ added as modules are ported)', which no longer reflects a tree containing src/service/, ~30 domain classes, ~40 data repositories, and 69 ui files. New engineers get a misleadingly tiny picture of the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Update the size to ~26 MB and refresh the Layout section to show the real top-level structure (src/data, src/domain, src/service, src/ui, tests/cases, packaging, sql) rather than the early-phase skeleton.

findings.title: No build/deploy troubleshooting or ICU-fallback caveats surfaced for operators
findings.detail: build-appimage.sh is excellently self-documented internally (glibc forward-compat, SQLite-only sqldrivers, ICU minimization with graceful full-library fallback). But none of these operational gotchas are surfaced in README/docs: e.g. that ICU minimization silently no-ops if icupkg/genccode/gcc are absent (yielding a much larger image), that the build must run on AlmaLinux 10 for portability, and there is no troubleshooting section for common deploy failures (missing xcb libs on target, FUSE/APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN, write permissions on ~/.local/share). The knowledge exists only as shell comments a deployer may never read.
findings.recommendation: Add a short 'Packaging & deploy troubleshooting' section to README (or docs/DEPLOY.md) lifting the key caveats from the script: build on oldest target, expected size with/without ICU tools, required runtime deps on the target, and first-run DB location/permissions.

findings.title: Live search runs a synchronous DB query on every keystroke (no debounce) on the three hottest screens
findings.detail: All three search boxes connect QLineEdit::textChanged directly to a slot that hits the DB and rebuilds the whole QTableWidget. PosTerminalPage connects textChanged -> runSearch (calls MedicineRepository::searchForPos, which runs two correlated subqueries over batches per matched medicine row plus a Barcode::parse). MedicinesPage connects textChanged -> reload (MedicineRepository::list, one correlated SUM subquery per row). InventoryPage connects textChanged -> reloadBatches. Typing 'paracetamol' fires 11 full searches, each scanning medicines with 5 LIKE predicates and per-row batch subqueries, plus a full QTableWidget teardown/rebuild and resizeRowsToContents on the main thread. On the POS terminal this is the single most-used input in the app and the one most sensitive to latency on the AlmaLinux target PC. At 318 meds it is tolerable but visibly laggy; it scales poorly and blocks the UI thread.
findings.recommendation: Debounce search with a single-shot QTimer (~150-200ms) restarted on each textChanged, firing the query only after typing pauses; or run the query on key release. Keep barcode scans snappy by also triggering immediately on returnPressed (already wired). This is the highest-ROI perf fix.

findings.title: No performance PRAGMAs and no ANALYZE — planner runs blind with tiny default cache
findings.detail: Database::open sets only PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON and journal_mode=WAL. Missing the standard single-PC tuning set: PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL (safe with WAL, far fewer fsyncs on every sale commit/audit insert), cache_size (default ~2MB page cache is small for report scans), mmap_size, and temp_store=MEMORY (report GROUP BY / ORDER BY and the velocity report spill temp b-trees to disk). There is also no ANALYZE ever run, so sqlite_stat tables are empty and the query planner picks indexes by heuristic only — risky for the multi-LIKE-OR search and the multi-join report queries where index choice matters. None of these change correctness; they are pure throughput wins on the exact write-heavy (sale commit) and scan-heavy (reports) paths flagged as critical in CLAUDE.md.
findings.recommendation: After open, set synchronous=NORMAL, cache_size (e.g. -16000 for ~16MB), temp_store=MEMORY, and a modest mmap_size. Run ANALYZE once at bootstrap and after the catalog import / periodically (or enable PRAGMA optimize on close). Verify synchronous=NORMAL+WAL durability is acceptable vs the crash-safety note in MEMORY.md.

findings.title: Report date filters wrap the indexed timestamp in date(col,'localtime'), defeating the index and forcing per-row conversion
findings.detail: Every date-ranged query filters with WHERE date(s.sold_at,'localtime') BETWEEN ? AND ?. Because the indexed column sold_at is wrapped in a function, the sales_sold_at / sales_cashier_sold_at indexes cannot be used — SQLite must full-scan sales (and joined sale_items) and call date() with timezone conversion on every row. The dashboard calls SalesReportRepository::report(today,today) on every load, so even the home screen pays a growing full scan as history accumulates. The velocity report (velocityReport) is the worst case: medicines LEFT JOIN sale_items LEFT JOIN sales with three CASE-WHEN date(...) SUMs per joined row over all time, GROUP BY medicine, HAVING another date() sum — a full cross-scan with no date predicate to prune.
findings.recommendation: Filter on a sargable expression: compute the stored-format datetime bounds in C++ (accounting for localtime offset) and use WHERE s.sold_at >= ? AND s.sold_at < ? so the sold_at index drives the scan; keep date() only in projection. For velocity, restrict the join to the last 90 days with a sargable predicate before grouping.

findings.title: No partial/filtered index for the repeated 'sellable batch' hot filter used by FEFO and on-hand subqueries
findings.detail: The recurring batch predicate current_qty>0 AND is_quarantined=0 AND is_expired=0 AND expiry_date>date('now') appears in searchForPos (twice per query, as correlated subqueries per medicine row), list (once per row), lowStock, expiringSoon and FEFO selection. The only batch indexes are (medicine_id, expiry_date), (expiry_date) and the unique (medicine_id, batch_number, expiry_date). batches_medicine_expiry covers the medicine_id+expiry lookup, but current_qty/is_quarantined/is_expired are not indexed, so each subquery still inspects every batch for that medicine and applies the flag/qty filters as residuals. With many batches per medicine over time this multiplies the per-keystroke cost.
findings.recommendation: Add a partial index targeting live, sellable stock, e.g. CREATE INDEX batches_sellable ON batches(medicine_id, expiry_date) WHERE current_qty>0 AND is_quarantined=0 AND is_expired=0. This shrinks the scanned set for FEFO and the search subqueries. Pair with the ANALYZE recommendation so the planner uses it.

findings.title: Analytics reports materialize unbounded result sets in C++ before truncating
findings.detail: To preserve exact Money math the analytics layer pulls raw rows and aggregates in C++ — correct for money fidelity, but several paths are unbounded. profitAndLoss builds every per-medicine row, sorts, then resizes to 500 (work done before the cap). taxReport, complianceReport, narcoticRegister and velocityReport have no LIMIT at all and return every matching row held in QVector + rendered into a QTableWidget. SalesReportRepository::report caps at 2000 rows but still loads all into memory and a widget. For a single pharmacy over a normal range this is fine, but a wide date range over years of data loads the entire history into RAM and a non-virtualized QTableWidget, which can stall the UI.
findings.recommendation: Push aggregation into SQL where money exactness allows (counts, GROUP BY for compliance/narcotic line lists), apply LIMITs to the detail reports, and consider QSqlQueryModel/virtualized views for large tabular results. At minimum cap and paginate the unbounded reports.

findings.title: Thermal print blocks the UI thread for up to 20 seconds on a slow/offline printer
findings.detail: CupsRawPrinter::printRaw launches `lp` via QProcess and synchronously blocks on waitForStarted(5000) then waitForFinished(15000) on the GUI thread (called directly from ReceiptDialog::printThermal). If the CUPS queue is paused, the printer is out of paper, or USB is disconnected, the cashier's entire app freezes for up to 20s with no feedback after every sale. This is the post-sale latency path; perceived POS responsiveness depends on it.
findings.recommendation: Show a non-blocking 'Sending to printer…' state and run the lp submission off the GUI thread (QtConcurrent or a worker), or reduce waitForFinished and report status asynchronously. At minimum give immediate UI feedback before blocking.

findings.title: No performance/regression coverage on the search and report query paths
findings.detail: The test suite thoroughly covers money/FEFO/stock correctness but has zero timing or large-dataset tests. There is no test that seeds the catalog to its real size (318 meds; MEMORY.md notes a pending 318-row seed) plus a realistic batch/sales volume and asserts that search and report queries stay within a budget or use the expected index (e.g. via EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN). The sargability and index regressions above would pass all existing tests silently.
findings.recommendation: Add a perf smoke test that seeds N medicines/batches/sales, asserts EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for the search and report queries uses an index (not SCAN), and optionally asserts a wall-clock budget with QElapsedTimer. This locks in the index/sargability fixes.

findings.title: Manager-PIN approval dialog breaks Enter-to-submit on a high-frequency flow
findings.detail: ManagerOverrideDialog calls UiUtil::makeScanSafe(this). makeScanSafe (UiUtil.cpp:46-84) installs an event filter that converts Enter in any QLineEdit into a Tab focus-advance and clears setDefault/setAutoDefault on every button, so a stray scanner Enter cannot submit. But this dialog is a manual PIN-approval prompt that fires on every discount and every controlled-substance sale. The cashier/manager types the PIN and naturally presses Enter to confirm — instead Enter just moves focus to the OK button, requiring a second Enter or Space. UiUtil.h:17 itself warns 'Do NOT use on dialogs where Enter-to-submit is intended (e.g. the login screen)'. This is exactly such a dialog: it has no scanner field worth protecting (PIN is keyed by a human), yet it pays the friction tax on the hottest authorization path.
findings.recommendation: Do not apply makeScanSafe to ManagerOverrideDialog (and ChangePinDialog). Instead wire returnPressed on the PIN field to accept() so a single Enter confirms, matching LoginDialog. If scanner protection is desired only on the optional license field, install the EnterAdvances filter on that field alone, not on the PIN.

findings.title: No accessibility metadata anywhere (setAccessibleName/Description absent)
findings.detail: A grep across all of src/ui for setAccessibleName / setAccessibleDescription returns zero hits. Many inputs (m_search, m_discount, m_tendered, m_pin) rely solely on placeholder text or an adjacent QFormLayout label for identification; placeholder text is not exposed as an accessible name and disappears once typing starts. Icon-only / chevron buttons (e.g. the 'Inventory ▾' QToolButton in MainWindow.cpp:146) and the QSpinBox-in-table qty controls in the cart have no accessible name. Screen readers and assistive tooling (and Qt's own automated UI testing) cannot reliably identify these controls. For a regulated medical-retail system this is a compliance-relevant gap.
findings.recommendation: Add setAccessibleName() (and where useful setAccessibleDescription) to the key POS and dialog inputs and to icon/chevron-only buttons. At minimum cover the POS terminal (search, discount, tendered, payment, cart qty cells, Complete sale) and all PIN/approval dialogs.

findings.title: Tab order is implicit (construction order), never set explicitly
findings.detail: No file in src/ui calls setTabOrder. Qt's default tab chain follows widget construction order, which here does not match the visual/logical order. In PosTerminalPage the widgets are constructed left-column-first (search, results, add buttons) then right-column (cart, remove/park buttons, then the discount/tendered/payment form, then Complete sale). A cashier tabbing from the search box will traverse the results table and left-side action buttons before reaching the checkout fields, rather than going search → (add) → discount → tendered → payment → complete. For a keyboard-driven POS the tab path through checkout is a core speed concern and is currently left to chance.
findings.recommendation: Define an explicit setTabOrder chain on PosTerminalPage (search → discount → tendered → payment → Complete sale, with the tables reachable but out of the primary checkout path) and on multi-field dialogs. Verify the resulting order by keyboard.

findings.title: PHP 'scan → auto-add to cart' speed flow not ported; no barcode/GS1 parsing on POS input
findings.detail: The PHP terminal (pos/frontend/pages/pos/terminal.php:47-81) parses a structured barcode into a 'searchChip', cleans the 50-char scanner string down to a clean GTIN, and auto-adds the matched medicine to the cart so the cashier gets 'scan → scan → scan → done' without ever clicking Add. The Qt port's runSearch() does a plain LIKE/text search and relies on the QLineEdit returnPressed handler (line 221-229) to add the first/highlighted row. There is no GS1 / Digital-Link / HIBC parsing wired into the POS search box (QrParser exists per PHP_APP_MAP but is not used here), so a structured barcode is fed verbatim into a text search and auto-add depends on the raw scan string happening to match. This loses the documented scan-throughput win and risks adding the wrong row for batch/expiry-encoded barcodes.
findings.recommendation: Run scanner input through the barcode parser before searching, and when input is recognized as a structured scan (not free-text), resolve to a single medicine and auto-add to the cart, mirroring terminal.php. Keep manual free-text search behavior unchanged.

findings.title: Cart re-render destroys/recreates qty spinboxes on every change, losing focus mid-edit
findings.detail: renderCart() does m_cart->setRowCount(0) then rebuilds every row and every QSpinBox cell widget from scratch (lines 342-377). recompute() is also called from each spinbox's valueChanged. Editing a qty (e.g. holding the stepper, or typing a multi-digit qty) can trigger a path that re-enters renderCart (e.g. after any other cart mutation), which deletes the spinbox the user is interacting with and rebuilds it, losing keyboard focus and the in-progress edit caret. While valueChanged alone only calls recompute (which does not rebuild), any add/remove/merge while a qty edit is pending will yank focus. This is jarring on a keyboard/touch POS.
findings.recommendation: Update existing rows in place where possible (set spinbox value and recompute totals) instead of tearing down the whole table on every change; only fully rebuild when the line set actually changes. Preserve the focused cell/widget across rebuilds when a rebuild is unavoidable.

findings.title: No touchscreen sizing for a retail-counter terminal
findings.detail: Controls use default desktop sizing. The cart qty QSpinBox sets only setMinimumWidth(72) (line 357) with default ~24px height and tiny up/down steppers; POS action buttons (Add unit, Complete sale) have no enlarged minimum height (contrast LoginDialog which at least sets 40px on Sign in). For a pharmacy counter where a touchscreen is plausible on AlmaLinux hardware, the qty steppers and primary actions are below comfortable touch-target size (~44px). The brief flags touchscreen suitability for this area.
findings.recommendation: If touch is a target, set larger minimum heights on POS primary actions and the cart qty control (or provide +/- buttons sized for touch). At minimum confirm with the deployment whether touch is in scope; if keyboard/mouse-only, document that decision.

findings.title: emptyState row can be mistaken for a real selectable result in selection-driven actions
findings.detail: emptyState() inserts a single spanned message row at row 0 with item flags Qt::ItemIsEnabled (not selectable), which correctly blocks selection. The POS guards addSelected() by checking item(row,0)->data(UserRole) presence (PosTerminalPage.cpp:285-289) so an empty-state row cannot be added — good. However the pattern is fragile and undocumented as a contract: any future selection-driven action that only checks 'item(row,0) != nullptr' (as the Alternatives enable check at line 202-203 effectively does) would treat the empty-state placeholder as a valid target, since the empty-state item is non-null. The enable check at line 202 is partially saved only because the empty-state row is non-selectable so currentRow stays -1, but this is incidental, not guaranteed.
findings.recommendation: Make the contract explicit: have emptyState tag its placeholder item (e.g. a known UserRole flag) and provide a UiUtil helper like isPlaceholderRow(table,row) that selection-driven code must consult, rather than relying on item-null or non-selectability side effects.

findings.title: Silent failure when POS pre-commit schedule query fails
findings.detail: In completeSale(), the query that loads controlled_schedule for the cart medicines is run with 'if (q.exec()) { ... }' (line 452) and the else branch is empty. If the query fails for any reason, the schedules list stays empty, needWitness/needLicense both become false, and the sale proceeds WITHOUT the controlled-substance witness/license gate and without any user-visible error. For a controlled-substance compliance control this is a silent fail-open: a UX/feedback gap that has regulatory consequences. There is no error state surfaced to the cashier.
findings.recommendation: On query failure, abort the sale and show a clear error (do not fail open on a compliance gate). Surface a QMessageBox::critical and keep the cart intact so the cashier can retry. Add a test that simulates the query failing and asserts the sale is blocked.

findings.title: Audit-log HMAC tamper-evidence chain dropped; columns are inert
findings.detail: db/triggers/audit_log_immutable.sql provides TWO guarantees: (1) append-only via BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE, and (2) an HMAC-SHA256 chain where each row's row_hmac = HMAC(secret, prev_hmac || canonical_payload), so dropping the trigger and forging history still fails verification. The SQLite port keeps only guarantee #1 (audit_log_no_update / audit_log_no_delete triggers in sql/schema_sqlite.sql:398-405). The prev_hmac/row_hmac columns exist (lines 386-387) but Audit::write (src/data/Audit.cpp:13-24) never populates them - they stay ''. CLAUDE.md says the HMAC chain may be simplified for single-PC SQLite but to keep the audit records, which the immutability trigger satisfies; however the schema comment at line 397 and Audit.h label it 'deferred to the Phase-6 Audit port', and Phase 6 has shipped (migrations reach v4) without it. Because there is no DB role separation, the triggers can be dropped via raw sqlite3, so without the chain there is no tamper-evidence - exactly the threat the PHP design addressed.
findings.recommendation: Either implement the HMAC chain (compute row_hmac on insert from prev tip + canonical payload using the same field order/pipe-join as the PHP audit_log_compute_hmac, keyed from AppPaths) and add a verifier, or formally accept the simplification in CLAUDE.md and remove the dead prev_hmac/row_hmac columns and 'deferred' comments so the schema does not imply a guarantee it never provides.

findings.title: z_report_archive immutability trigger not ported (regulatory evidence is mutable)
findings.detail: db/triggers/phase5_drap.sql creates z_report_archive AND a prevent_z_report_archive_modifications BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE trigger ('A day-close record is a regulator's evidence; rewriting it is a control breach'). The SQLite port creates the table in migration v2 (src/data/Database.cpp:205-212) with NO immutability trigger. ZReportArchive::signAndStore uses INSERT OR IGNORE (append-once) so the app does not rewrite, but nothing at the DB level blocks a raw UPDATE/DELETE of an archived, HMAC-signed day-close report. This is the same append-only guarantee that WAS ported for audit_log but silently omitted here.
findings.recommendation: Add CREATE TRIGGER z_report_archive_no_update / _no_delete BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE ... RAISE(ABORT) mirroring the audit_log triggers, in the migration that creates the table (or a new migration). Cover it with the same rejects() pattern used for audit_log in tests/cases/schema_tests.cpp.

findings.title: One-open-session-per-cashier partial-unique index dropped; only racy app check remains
findings.detail: db/triggers/phase9_concurrency_hardening.sql adds a partial UNIQUE INDEX cashier_sessions_one_open_per_user ON cashier_sessions(cashier_id) WHERE status='OPEN' as the DB 'suspenders' behind the app-side check. This index is absent from sql/schema_sqlite.sql and every migration. SessionRepository::openSession (src/data/SessionRepository.cpp:51) does a read-then-insert with the openSessionId() check at the start, before the transaction, so two near-simultaneous opens (double-click, or a retried op) can both pass the SELECT and insert two OPEN sessions, splitting totals across two shifts. On single PC the window is small but the DB guard is exactly what the PHP authors added because the app check raced in live QA.
findings.recommendation: Port the partial-unique index as a migration: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS cashier_sessions_one_open_per_user ON cashier_sessions(cashier_id) WHERE status='OPEN'. Then the duplicate INSERT fails atomically and openSession can surface the friendly message on the constraint error. Add a test.

findings.title: parked_carts lost its foreign key - orphaned carts on user delete
findings.detail: In Postgres (db/triggers/phase8_pos_customer_and_parked.sql) parked_carts.cashier_id is BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE CASCADE. The SQLite port (sql/schema_sqlite.sql:425-433) declares parked_carts.cashier_id as a plain nullable INTEGER with no NOT NULL and no FOREIGN KEY clause at all. Consequences: (1) a parked cart can reference a deleted/soft-deleted user with no cascade cleanup, leaving stale parked bills that still surface in the cashier's parked list; (2) referential integrity between parked_carts and users is unenforced even with foreign_keys=ON. The branch_id column also has no FK, a lesser inconsistency.
findings.recommendation: Add FOREIGN KEY (cashier_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE (and optionally branch_id REFERENCES branches(id)). Since the table is in the baseline, add the FK via a table-rebuild migration (SQLite cannot ALTER ADD CONSTRAINT) or recreate it in a migration. Verify ParkedCartRepository handles the cascade.

findings.title: No busy_timeout under WAL; concurrent writers fail immediately with SQLITE_BUSY
findings.detail: Database::open (src/data/Database.cpp:26-27) sets PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON and journal_mode=WAL but never sets PRAGMA busy_timeout (or the QSQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT connect option). With WAL there can legitimately be a second connection (a checkpoint, a background/export task, or a future second QSqlDatabase handle); any writer that hits a held write lock gets an immediate 'database is locked' error and the wrapping transaction rolls back rather than waiting. The PHP/Postgres design explicitly used lock_timeout=5s (phase6_db_hardening.sql) to bound, not eliminate, lock waits. Single-PC risk is low but a transient lock would surface to the cashier as a failed sale.
findings.recommendation: Set a busy timeout on open, e.g. m_db.setConnectOptions("QSQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT=5000") before open(), or PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000 alongside the other pragmas, to match the 5s lock_timeout intent.

findings.title: Receipt-number generation has a COUNT-based race with a non-monotonic random fallback
findings.detail: SaleService::nextReceiptNumber (src/service/SaleService.cpp:29-53) builds INV-YYYYMMDD-NNNN from COUNT(*) of today's sales + 1, then on collision falls back to a random 6-digit suffix. Because the count read is not part of the inserting transaction's serialization point and voided/refunded rows still count, two sales racing (or a retry) can compute the same candidate; the sales_receipt_number_key UNIQUE index correctly prevents a true duplicate, but the fallback then produces a non-sequential receipt number (INV-YYYYMMDD-<random>) that breaks the otherwise monotonic daily sequence operators/regulators expect. The UNIQUE index is the real safety net (good), but the numbering scheme degrades under contention.
findings.recommendation: Generate the receipt number inside the sale transaction and prefer a per-day monotonic source (MAX(suffix)+1 parsed from today's receipt_number, or a small per-day counter row) rather than COUNT(*); keep the UNIQUE index as the backstop. If the random fallback is retained, log it so a gap/odd number is explainable in an audit.

findings.title: Dropped DB invariants (z_report immutability, one-open-session, parked_carts FK) have no tests
findings.detail: schema_tests.cpp covers what WAS ported well: foreign_keys=ON, role/controlled_schedule/tax_code CHECKs, batches.current_qty/received_qty>=0, batches.medicine_id FK, medicines partial-unique live SKU + reuse-after-soft-delete, and audit_log UPDATE/DELETE-blocked. But there is no test asserting the absent invariants, so their omission was never caught: no test that z_report_archive rejects UPDATE/DELETE, no test that a cashier cannot have two OPEN sessions, no test that deleting a user cascades/blocks parked_carts, and no general FK cascade-on-delete coverage (e.g. sale_items deleted with their sale; returns RESTRICT). CLAUDE.md mandates tests on the stock/expiry/integrity paths.
findings.recommendation: Add schema/integration tests for: z_report_archive immutability (after porting the trigger), the one-open-session constraint, parked_carts FK cascade on user delete, and at least one ON DELETE CASCADE (sale_items) and one ON DELETE RESTRICT (returns->sales) assertion. These tests lock in the fixes above and guard against future schema regressions.
